title.zh: 卷三十五 列傳第二十五 劉湛 庾悅 顧琛 顧覬之
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 25: Liu Zhan, Yu Yue, Gu Chen, Gu Jizhi
title.raw: 卷三十五 列傳第二十五 劉湛 庾悅 顧琛 顧覬之 Volume 35 Biographies 25: Liu Zhan, Yu Yue, Gu Chen, Gu Jizhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十五

translations.literal: Biographies 25
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Number Twenty-Five

sentences.zh: 劉湛庾悅顧琛顧覬之

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, Yu Yue, Gu Chen, and Gu Jizhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan · Yu Yue · Gu Chen · Gu Jizhi

sentences.zh: 除宋武帝太尉行參軍，賞遇甚厚。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Adjutant to the Grand Commandant under Emperor Wu of Song, and was rewarded and treated with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Song's founding emperor appointed him acting adjutant on the Grand Commandant's staff, where he enjoyed lavish favor.

sentences.zh: 父柳亡于江州，府州送故甚豐，一無所受，時論稱之。

translations.literal: When his father Liu died in Jiang Province, the prefecture and provincial offices sent funeral gifts in great abundance, yet he accepted none of it; contemporaries praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: After his father Liu died in Jiang Province, the prefectural and provincial offices sent lavish funeral gifts; he refused every item, and public opinion praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為相國參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became an aide to the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Once his mourning period ended, he served as an aide to the Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 謝晦、王弘並稱其器幹。

translations.literal: Xie Hui and Wang Hong both praised his capacity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Both Xie Hui and Wang Hong spoke highly of his talent and executive skill.

sentences.zh: 武帝入受晉命，以第四子義康為冠軍將軍、豫州刺史，留鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu entered to receive the Jin mandate, he made his fourth son Yikang General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yu Province, leaving him to garrison Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu accepted the Jin throne's transfer of mandate, he posted his fourth son Yikang as General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yu Province, garrisoned at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 以湛為長史、梁郡太守。

translations.literal: Zhan was made Chief Administrator and Administrator of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was appointed chief administrator to the prince and concurrently Administrator of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 義康弱年未親政，府州事悉委湛。

translations.literal: Yikang was young and had not yet personally handled government; all prefectural and provincial affairs were entrusted to Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang was still a youth and did not yet govern in person; Zhan handled every matter of the prefecture and province.

sentences.zh: 進號右將軍，仍隨府轉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Right and continued to follow the prince's transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to General of the Right, he moved whenever the prince's headquarters moved.

sentences.zh: 義康以本號徙南豫州，湛改領曆陽太守。

translations.literal: When Yikang moved to Southern Yu Province under his original title, Zhan was changed to concurrently administer Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang transferred to Southern Yu Province under his existing title, Zhan took concurrent command as Administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 為人剛嚴用法，奸吏犯贓百錢以上皆殺之，自下莫不震肅。

translations.literal: As a man he was stern and strict in applying the law; corrupt officials guilty of embezzlement of a hundred cash or more were all put to death, and from the lowest ranks upward none failed to be awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Hard and severe in enforcing the law, he executed any corrupt clerk who embezzled as little as a hundred cash; terror ran from the bottom of the bureaucracy to the top.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王義真出為車騎將軍、南豫州刺史，湛又為長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Prince of Luling Yizhen went out as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Southern Yu Province, Zhan again became Chief Administrator, his post as Administrator remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Luling Yizhen left court as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Southern Yu Province, Zhan again served as chief administrator while retaining his post as administrator.

sentences.zh: 義真時居武帝憂，使帳下備膳，湛禁之，義真乃使左右人買魚肉珍羞，於齋內別立廚帳。

translations.literal: Yizhen was then in mourning for Emperor Wu and had his attendants prepare meals; Zhan forbade it, so Yizhen had his attendants buy fish, meat, and delicacies and set up a separate kitchen tent within the mourning hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was observing mourning for Emperor Wu and ordered his staff to prepare food; Zhan forbade it, so Yizhen had attendants buy fish, meat, and delicacies and erect a separate kitchen inside the mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 會湛入，因命臑酒炙車螯。

translations.literal: When Zhan happened to enter, he thereupon ordered cured meat, wine, and roasted mantis shrimp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan entered unexpectedly and was served cured meats, wine, and roasted mantis shrimp.

sentences.zh: 湛正色曰：「公當今不宜有此設。

translations.literal: Zhan said with a stern face: "Your Grace ought not to have such an arrangement at present."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said gravely, "Your Grace should not be entertaining like this while in mourning."

sentences.zh: 」義真曰：「旦甚寒，杯酒亦何傷，長史事同一家，望不為異。

translations.literal: Yizhen said: "The morning is very cold; a cup of wine—what harm? The Chief Administrator and I are as one household; I hope you will not take it amiss."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen replied, "The morning is bitter cold—a cup of wine can hardly hurt. We are family, Chief Administrator; please do not stand on ceremony."

sentences.zh: 」酒至，湛起曰：「既不能以禮自處，又不能以禮處人。」

translations.literal: When the wine arrived, Zhan rose and said: "Since you cannot conduct yourself by ritual, neither can you treat others by ritual."
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was served, Zhan stood and said, "You cannot keep ritual toward yourself, and you cannot keep it toward others either."

sentences.zh: 後為廣州刺史，嫡母憂去職。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Guang Province and left office on mourning for his principal mother.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Inspector of Guang Province and resigned when his principal mother died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為侍中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時王華、王曇首、殷景仁亦為侍中，文帝於合殿與四人宴飲甚悅。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, and Yin Jingren were also Palace Attendants; Emperor Wen feasted and drank with the four men in the Hall of Assembly and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, and Yin Jingren were also Palace Attendants at the time; Emperor Wen dined with all four in the Hall of Assembly and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 華等出，帝目送良久，歎曰：「此四賢一時之秀，同管喉唇，恐後世難繼。

translations.literal: When Hua and the others left, the Emperor watched them go for a long time and sighed: "These four worthies are the finest of their age, together managing the throat and lips; I fear later ages will find them hard to match."
translations.idiomatic: As they left, the emperor watched them a long while and sighed, "Four brilliant men at once, all guarding the emperor's voice—I doubt posterity will see their like again."

sentences.zh: 」及撫軍將軍江夏王義恭鎮江陵，以湛為使持節、南蠻校尉，領撫軍長史，行府州事。

translations.literal: When General Who Pacifies the Army Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was stationed at Jiangling, Zhan was made Bearer of the Staff, Colonel of Southern Barbarians, Chief Administrator to the Pacifying Army, and charged with prefectural and provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, General Who Pacifies the Army, took Jiangling, Zhan received the staff of office as Colonel of Southern Barbarians, chief administrator to the Pacifying Army, and acting head of the prefecture and province.

sentences.zh: 王弘輔政，而王華、王曇首任事居中，湛自謂才能不後之，不願外出。

translations.literal: Wang Hong assisted in government, while Wang Hua and Wang Tanshou held power at court; Zhan considered his talent not inferior to theirs and was unwilling to go out on assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong governed as regent while Wang Hua and Wang Tanshou held real power at court; Zhan believed himself their equal in talent and refused to accept an outside posting.

sentences.zh: 是行也，謂為弘等所斥，意甚不平。

translations.literal: On this assignment he believed himself expelled by Hong and the others, and his resentment ran very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He took the transfer as a banishment engineered by Hong and his circle, and nursed a deep grievance.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「二王若非代邸之舊，無以至此。

translations.literal: He often said: "Had the two Wangs not been old associates from the Prince of Dai's household, they would never have reached this point."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "If the two Wangs had not been old companions from the Prince of Dai's household, they would never have risen so high."

sentences.zh: 可謂遭遇風雲。

translations.literal: One might call it meeting with wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: They had simply ridden the storm, he meant.

sentences.zh: 」湛負其才氣，常慕汲黯、崔琰為人，故名長子曰黯字長孺，第二子曰琰字季珪。

translations.literal: Zhan, relying on his talent and spirit, always admired Ji An and Cui Yan as men; therefore he named his eldest son An, courtesy name Changru, and his second son Yan, courtesy name Jigui.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his own gifts, Zhan modeled himself on the Han minister Ji An and the Wei statesman Cui Yan; he named his eldest son An (Changru) and his second Yan (Jigui).

sentences.zh: 琰於江陵病卒，湛求自送喪還都，義恭亦為之陳情。

translations.literal: When Yan died of illness at Jiangling, Zhan requested leave to escort the coffin back to the capital; Yigong also pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan died at Jiangling, Zhan asked permission to escort the coffin to the capital, and Yigong petitioned on his behalf as well.

sentences.zh: 文帝答義恭曰：「吾亦得湛啟事，為之酸懷，乃不欲苟違所請；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen replied to Yigong: "I too have received Zhan's memorial and am pained at heart; I do not wish lightly to deny his request;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen answered Yigong, "I too have Zhan's petition, and it wrings my heart—I do not wish to refuse him lightly;

sentences.zh: 但汝弱年，新涉軍務，八州殷曠，專斷事重，疇諮委仗，不可不得其人。

translations.literal: but you are young and newly involved in military affairs; the eight provinces are vast, and sole decision-making is weighty—whom to consult and rely upon cannot be anyone but the right man.
translations.idiomatic: but you are young and new to military command. Eight provinces are vast, and sole discretion is a heavy burden—you cannot do without the right adviser at your side.

sentences.zh: 量算二三，未獲便相順許。

translations.literal: After weighing the matter two or three times, I cannot immediately grant consent.
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed the matter again and again and cannot grant it just yet.

sentences.zh: 今答湛啟，權停彼葬。

translations.literal: In answering Zhan's memorial I temporarily defer the burial there.
translations.idiomatic: My reply to Zhan will defer the burial for the moment.

sentences.zh: 頃朝臣零落相系，寄懷轉寡，湛實國器，吾乃欲引其令還，直以西夏任重，要且停此事耳。

translations.literal: Recently court ministers have fallen one after another; those in whom I can confide grow fewer. Zhan is truly a pillar of the state—I intend to summon him back; only because the western defense is weighty must this matter wait for now.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers have been dying in succession, and trusted confidants grow scarce. Zhan is truly a pillar of the realm and I mean to recall him—but the western frontier is too important to release him yet.

sentences.zh: 汝慶賞黜罰預關得失者，必宜悉相委寄。」

translations.literal: In matters of reward, punishment, promotion, and dismissal that touch gain and loss, you must entrust them entirely to him."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever touches reward, punishment, promotion, or dismissal, you must leave entirely in his hands."

sentences.zh: 義恭性甚狷隘，年又漸大，欲專政事，每為湛所裁。

translations.literal: Yigong's nature was very narrow and jealous; as he grew older he wished to monopolize government, and Zhan constantly checked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was narrow and jealous; as he aged he wanted sole control of affairs, and Zhan repeatedly overruled him.

sentences.zh: 主佐之間，嫌隙遂構。

translations.literal: Between lord and aide, resentment was thus formed.
translations.idiomatic: Between prince and chief administrator, enmity took root.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞之，密遣詰讓義恭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen heard of it, he secretly sent someone to rebuke Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen heard of the friction and secretly sent a messenger to reprove Yigong.

sentences.zh: 義恭陳湛無居下之禮，又自以年長，未得行意，雖奉詔旨，每出怨言。

translations.literal: Yigong reported that Zhan lacked the decorum of a subordinate, and he also considered himself older and unable to carry out his intentions; though he obeyed the imperial edict, he often uttered complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong complained that Zhan showed no subordinate's deference; feeling himself the elder and unable to govern as he wished, he obeyed the edict in form but grumbled constantly.

sentences.zh: 上友于素篤，欲加酬順，乃詔之曰：「當今之才，委受已爾，宜盡相彌縫，取其可取，棄其可棄。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's brotherly affection had always been deep, and wishing to reconcile them further, he issued an edict saying: "Among present talents, delegation has already been made thus; you should fully mend matters together, take what can be taken, and discard what can be discarded."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's affection for his brother ran deep; seeking further harmony, he ordered, "Talents have already been assigned as they are—you must patch things up, keep what is worth keeping, and drop what must be dropped."

sentences.zh: 先是王華既亡，曇首又卒，領軍將軍殷景仁以時賢零落，白文帝征湛。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Hua had died and Tanshou had also passed away; General of the Palace Guard Yin Jingren, seeing worthy men falling away, informed Emperor Wen to summon Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Hua's death and Tanshou's passing, Palace Guard General Yin Jingren, alarmed at the thinning ranks of talent, urged Emperor Wen to recall Zhan.

sentences.zh: 八年，召為太子詹事，加給事中，與景仁並被任遇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent with additional appointment as Supervising Censor, and he and Jingren were both favored with trust.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent with additional rank as Supervising Censor; he and Jingren shared the emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 湛云：「今代宰相何難，此正可當我南陽郡漢代功曹耳。

translations.literal: Zhan said: "Replacing the Chancellor today—what difficulty is that? This is exactly like my Han-era post as Merit Officer in Nanyang Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan remarked, "Serving as de facto chancellor now—what is so hard about that? It is no more than being merit officer in Nanyang Commandery under the Han."

sentences.zh: 」明年，景仁轉尚書僕射，領選，護軍將軍，湛代為領軍。

translations.literal: The next year Jingren transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently overseeing selection and as General Who Protects the Army; Zhan replaced him as General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jingren became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, overseeing appointments and General Who Protects the Army; Zhan replaced him as General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 十二年，又領詹事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he also concurrently held the Grand Tutor's post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he also retained the post of Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 湛與景仁素款，又以其建議征之，甚相感悅。

translations.literal: Zhan and Jingren had long been on intimate terms, and because Jingren had recommended summoning him, they were deeply pleased with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and Jingren had been close friends, and Zhan was deeply grateful that Jingren had urged his recall.

sentences.zh: 及俱被時遇，猜隙漸生。

translations.literal: Once both were favored by the times, suspicion and rifts gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: Once both stood in favor at court, suspicion and friction slowly grew.

sentences.zh: 以景仁專內任，謂為間己。

translations.literal: Because Jingren monopolized inner appointments, Zhan considered it interference against himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren controlled inner appointments, and Zhan took it as a move against him.

sentences.zh: 時彭城王義康專執朝權，而湛昔為上佐，遂以舊情委心自結，欲因宰相之力回主心，傾黜景仁，獨當時務。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Pengcheng Yikang monopolized court power; Zhan, having once been his chief aide, therefore bound himself to him with old affection, wishing through the Chancellor's power to turn the Emperor's heart, overthrow and dismiss Jingren, and alone handle affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang then dominated the court. Zhan, once his chief administrator, pledged himself to the prince in old friendship, hoping through the chancellor's power to sway the emperor, oust Jingren, and run affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 義康屢言之于文帝，其事不行。

translations.literal: Yikang repeatedly spoke of this to Emperor Wen, but the matter did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang repeatedly pressed the case before Emperor Wen, but the emperor would not act.

sentences.zh: 義康僚屬及湛諸附隸潛相約勒，無敢曆殷氏門者。

translations.literal: Yikang's staff and all Zhan's followers secretly agreed among themselves that none dared pass through the Yin family's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang's staff and Zhan's followers secretly agreed that no one was to visit the Yin household.

sentences.zh: 湛党劉敬文父成未悟其機，詣景仁求郡，敬文遽謝湛曰：「老父悖耄，遂就殷鐵幹祿。

translations.literal: Zhan's partisan Liu Jingwen's father Cheng had not grasped the scheme and went to Jingren seeking a commandery post; Jingwen hastily apologized to Zhan: "My old father is muddled in his dotage and went to Iron Yin for an office and salary."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cheng, father of Zhan's ally Liu Jingwen, failed to read the situation and visited Jingren to ask for a prefecture; Jingwen rushed to apologize to Zhan, "My old father, senile and confused, went begging office from 'Iron' Yin."

sentences.zh: 由敬文闇淺，上負生成，合門慚懼，無地自處。

translations.literal: Because Jingwen is shallow and dark, I have failed the grace shown me above; the whole household is ashamed and fearful, with no place to hide our faces.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen is dull and shallow; I have betrayed the grace shown us from above. Our whole house is ashamed and terrified, with nowhere to hide our faces.

sentences.zh: 」敬文之奸諂如此。

translations.literal: Thus was Jingwen's sycophantic treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the flattery and treachery of Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 義康擅權專朝，威傾內外，湛愈推崇之，無復人臣之禮，上稍不能平。

translations.literal: Yikang usurped power and monopolized the court; his authority tilted inside and outside. Zhan increasingly exalted him, no longer observing a minister's decorum, and the Emperor gradually grew displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang seized power and dominated court and countryside alike; Zhan exalted him ever more openly, abandoning a minister's decorum, and the emperor's displeasure mounted.

sentences.zh: 湛初入朝，委任甚重，善論政道，並諳前代故事，聽者忘疲。

translations.literal: When Zhan first entered court he was entrusted with great responsibility; he was skilled at discussing government and thoroughly versed in precedents of former ages, and listeners forgot fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan first came to court he bore heavy trust; he debated policy with ease and knew former dynasties' precedents by heart, and listeners forgot their weariness.

sentences.zh: 每入雲龍門，禦者便解駕，左右及羽儀隨意分散，不夕不出，以此為常。

translations.literal: Each time he entered the Cloud Dragon Gate the imperial driver would unharness the carriage; attendants and guard of honor dispersed as they pleased, and he did not leave before evening—this became his custom.
translations.idiomatic: Each entry through the Cloud Dragon Gate ended with the imperial driver unharnessing the horses; attendants and guard of honor wandered off at will, and he rarely left before nightfall.

sentences.zh: 及晚節驅煽義康，陵轢朝廷，上意雖內離而接遇不改。

translations.literal: In his later years he incited Yikang and rode roughshod over the court; though the Emperor inwardly turned away, his reception of Zhan did not change.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he fanned Yikang's ambitions and trampled the court; though the emperor's heart had turned against him, his outward courtesy never changed.

sentences.zh: 上謂所親曰：「劉斑初自西還，吾與語常看日早晚，慮其當去；

translations.literal: The Emperor said to those close to him: "When Ban the Liu first returned from the west, whenever I spoke with him I watched whether the sun was early or late, fearing he would leave;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told intimates, "When Liu Ban first returned from the west, I always watched the sun while we talked, afraid he would leave;

sentences.zh: 比入亦看日早晚，慮其不去。

translations.literal: now when he enters I also watch whether the sun is early or late, fearing he will not leave."
translations.idiomatic: now when he comes in I watch the sun just as closely, afraid he will not leave."

sentences.zh: 」湛小字斑獸，故云斑也。

translations.literal: Zhan's childhood name was Banshou, hence he said Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's childhood name was Banshou—hence "Ban."

sentences.zh: 遷丹陽尹，詹事如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Danyang, retaining his post as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Intendant of Danyang while keeping the Grand Tutorship.

sentences.zh: 十七年，所生母亡。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year his birth mother died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year his birth mother died.

sentences.zh: 上與義康形跡既乖，釁難將結，湛亦知無復全地。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Yikang had already grown estranged in conduct; disaster was about to be tied; Zhan also knew there was no longer any safe ground.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and Yikang had already drifted apart; catastrophe was near, and Zhan knew he could no longer keep his footing.

sentences.zh: 及至丁艱，謂所親曰：「今年必敗，常日賴口舌爭之，故得推遷耳。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning he said to those close to him: "This year I am sure to fall; on ordinary days I relied on disputing with my tongue, and so was able to gain deferment.
translations.idiomatic: Entering mourning, he told intimates, "I am finished this year. On ordinary days I talked my way out of trouble and bought delay.

sentences.zh: 今既窮毒，無復此望，禍至其能久乎。

translations.literal: Now that I am utterly poisoned, I have no further hope of this—when disaster comes, can it long endure?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I am trapped in mourning with no such hope left—when ruin arrives, how long can it wait?"

sentences.zh: 」伏甲於室，以待上臨吊。

translations.literal: He hid armed men in his chamber, waiting for the Emperor to come in person to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: He posted armed men in his house, waiting for the emperor to come in person to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 謀又泄，竟弗之幸。

translations.literal: The plot again leaked out, and in the end the Emperor did not visit.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked again, and the emperor never came.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔收付廷尉，於獄伏誅，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict ordered his arrest and delivery to the Court of Justice; he was executed in prison at age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict ordered his arrest and trial; he was executed in prison at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子黯等從誅。

translations.literal: His sons An and the others were executed with him.
translations.idiomatic: His sons An and the others were executed along with him.

sentences.zh: 弟素，黃門郎，徙廣州。

translations.literal: His younger brother Su, a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, was banished to Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Su, a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, was exiled to Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 湛初被收，歎曰：「便是亂邪。

translations.literal: When Zhan was first arrested he sighed: "So this is rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: At his arrest Zhan sighed, "So this counts as rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「不言無我應亂，殺我日自是亂法耳。

translations.literal: He also said: "Not to say that without me there ought to be rebellion—on the day they kill me, that itself will be rebellion against the law."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I won't claim that without me the realm would revolt—but the day they kill me, the law itself will have rebelled."

sentences.zh: 」入獄見素，曰：「乃復及汝邪？

translations.literal: Entering prison and seeing Su, he said: "So you too are implicated?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Su in prison he said, "You too?"

sentences.zh: 相勸為惡，惡不可為，相勸為善，正見今日，如何！

translations.literal: When others urged doing evil, evil cannot be done; when others urged doing good, this is exactly what we see today—how is that?
translations.idiomatic: When men urged evil, I knew evil must not be done; when they urged good, look where good has brought us today—what then?"

sentences.zh: 」湛生女輒殺之，為時流所怪。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhan bore a daughter he killed her; men of the age found this strange.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan killed every daughter born to him—a practice contemporaries found bizarre.

sentences.zh: 庾悅字仲豫，潁川鄢陵人也，晉太尉亮之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yu Yue, courtesy name Zhongyu, was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan, great-grandson of Jin Grand Commandant Yu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue, styled Zhongyu, came from Yanling in Yingchuan Commandery and was great-grandson of Jin Grand Commandant Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 祖羲，吳興內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi was Interior Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi served as Interior Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父准，西中郎將、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zhun was General of the Right in the Center and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhun was General of the Right in the Center and Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 悅仕晉為司徒右長史。

translations.literal: Yue served Jin as Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, Yue served as Right Chief Administrator on the Minister of Education's staff.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, he became Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized the throne, he became a Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宋武平建鄴，累遷建威將軍、江州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When Song Wu pacified Jiankang, he was repeatedly promoted to General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Jiang Province, with additional command as Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Song's founding emperor pacified Jiankang, Yue rose to General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Jiang Province with area command.

sentences.zh: 初，劉毅家在京口，酷貧，嘗與鄉曲士大夫往東堂共射，時悅為司徒右長史，要府州僚佐出東堂，毅已先至，遣與悅相聞曰：「身並貧躓，營一遊甚難。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Yi's family was at Jingkou and was extremely poor; he once went with local gentry to the Eastern Hall to shoot together. At that time Yue was Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education and had invited prefectural and provincial staff to the Eastern Hall; Yi had already arrived first and sent word to Yue: "We are alike in poverty and hardship; arranging one outing is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Liu Yi's household at Jingkou was desperately poor, he went with local gentlemen to shoot at the Eastern Hall. Yue, then Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education, had invited prefectural staff there; Yi arrived first and sent word: "We are both poor men for whom an outing is a rare luxury.

sentences.zh: 君如意人，無處不可為適，豈不能以此堂見讓。

translations.literal: You are a man who gets his way; nowhere is unsuitable for you—could you not yield this hall to us?"
translations.idiomatic: You are a man who always finds comfort—surely you can spare us this hall?"

sentences.zh: 」悅素豪，徑前不答。

translations.literal: Yue was by nature overbearing; he went straight forward and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was proud by nature; he walked past without a word.

sentences.zh: 毅語眾人並避，唯毅留射如故。

translations.literal: Yi told the others all to withdraw; only Yi remained shooting as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yi told the others to leave; only he kept shooting.

sentences.zh: 悅廚饌甚盛，不以及毅，毅既不去，悅甚不歡。

translations.literal: Yue's kitchen fare was very lavish and did not extend to Yi; since Yi would not leave, Yue was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's feast was lavish but excluded Yi; Yi refused to go, and Yue was furious.

sentences.zh: 毅又相聞曰：「身今年未得子鵝，豈能以殘炙見惠。

translations.literal: Yi again sent word: "This year I have not obtained young geese—how could I offer you leftover roast?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent another message: "I haven't got young geese this year—surely you don't expect me to treat you to scraps?"

sentences.zh: 」悅又不答。

translations.literal: Yue again did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yue again said nothing.

sentences.zh: 至是，毅表解悅都督、將軍官，以刺史移鎮豫章。

translations.literal: At this time Yi memorialized to remove Yue's posts as Area Commander and General and, as Inspector, moved his headquarters to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yi memorialized to strip Yue of his command and general's rank and, as inspector, transferred him to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 以親將趙恢領千兵守尋陽，建威府文武三千人悉入毅將府，深相挫辱。

translations.literal: He had his close general Zhao Hui lead a thousand troops to garrison Xunyang; three thousand civil and military staff of the Establishing Might headquarters all entered Yi's general's staff, and Yue was deeply humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: Yi posted his confidant Zhao Hui with a thousand men at Xunyang and absorbed all three thousand staff of Yue's headquarters into his own command, humiliating Yue thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 悅不得志，疽發背，到豫章少日卒。

translations.literal: Yue did not achieve his ambition; a carbuncle broke out on his back, and a few days after reaching Yuzhang he died.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his ambitions, Yue developed a back abscess and died within days of reaching Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 登之字元龍，悅族弟也。

translations.literal: Dengzhi, courtesy name Yuanlong, was Yue's clansman younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi, styled Yuanlong, was Yue's clansman and junior kinsman.

sentences.zh: 曾祖冰，晉司空。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Bing was Jin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Bing had been Jin Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 祖蘊，廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun was Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun served as Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 父廓，東陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Kuo was Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuo was Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 登之少以強濟自立，初為宋武帝鎮軍參軍，預討桓玄功，封曲江縣五等男。

translations.literal: Dengzhi in youth relied on force and resourcefulness to establish himself; he first became an aide to Song Wu's Pacifying Army, shared in the merit of suppressing Huan Xuan, and was enfeoffed as Fifth-rank Baron of Qujiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Dengzhi made his way by force of will and practical skill; he first served on Song Wu's Pacifying Army staff, earned merit in the campaign against Huan Xuan, and was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Baron of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 累遷新安太守。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts to Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 謝晦為荊州刺史，請為長史、南郡太守，仍為衛軍長史。

translations.literal: When Xie Hui became Inspector of Jing Province, he requested Dengzhi as Chief Administrator and Administrator of Nan Commandery, and he also served as Chief Administrator to the Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui became Inspector of Jing Province he took Dengzhi as chief administrator and Administrator of Nan Commandery, and later as chief administrator to the Guard General.

sentences.zh: 登之與晦俱曹氏婿，名位本同，一旦為之佐，意甚不愜。

translations.literal: Dengzhi and Hui were both sons-in-law of the Cao family; their names and ranks had originally been equal, yet suddenly to become his aide—his mind was very discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi and Hui were both sons-in-law of the Cao clan and had once stood on equal footing; to become Hui's subordinate overnight rankled deeply.

sentences.zh: 到廳箋唯言：「即日恭到」，初無感謝之言。

translations.literal: When he arrived at the hall his memorial of arrival said only: "Respectfully arrived this day"—at first there was no word of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: At the reception hall his arrival note read only, "Arrived today with respect"—not a word of thanks.

sentences.zh: 每入覲見，備持箱囊幾席之屬，一物不具，則不肯坐。

translations.literal: Each time he entered for audience he fully prepared chests, bags, stools, and mats; if one item was lacking he would not sit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended audience he brought his own chests, bags, stools, and mats; if one item was missing he refused to sit.

sentences.zh: 嘗於晦坐誦西征賦云：「生有修短之命，位有通塞之遇。

translations.literal: Once at Hui's seat he recited from the Rhapsody on the Western Expedition: "Life has the fate of long and short; rank has the encounter of smooth and blocked."
translations.idiomatic: Once in Hui's presence he recited from the Rhapsody on the Western Expedition: "Life grants long or short spans; office brings smooth fortune or blocked paths."

sentences.zh: 」晦雖恨而常優容之。

translations.literal: Though Hui resented it he always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Hui resented the barb but always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 晦拒王師，欲登之留守，登之不許。

translations.literal: When Hui resisted the imperial army and wished Dengzhi to remain behind on garrison duty, Dengzhi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui resisted the imperial army and asked Dengzhi to hold the rear, Dengzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 晦敗，登之以無任免官禁錮還家。

translations.literal: When Hui was defeated, Dengzhi was dismissed from office for incompetence, confined, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's defeat Dengzhi was dismissed for incompetence, placed under house arrest, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 何承天戲之曰：「因禍為福，未必皆知。

translations.literal: He Chengtian joked with him: "Turning calamity into blessing—not everyone knows how."
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian teased him, "Turning disaster into blessing—not everyone understands that art."

sentences.zh: 」登之曰：「我亦幾與三豎同戮。

translations.literal: Dengzhi said: "I too nearly shared execution with the three wretches."
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi replied, "I nearly died with those three wretches myself."

sentences.zh: 」承天為晦作表云：「當浮舟東下，戮此三豎。

translations.literal: Chengtian had written a memorial for Hui saying: "I shall float my boat eastward and slaughter these three wretches."
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian had drafted Hui's memorial saying, "I shall sail east and cut down these three wretches."

sentences.zh: 」故登之為嘲。

translations.literal: Hence Dengzhi's mockery.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Dengzhi's jest.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education and Administrator of Southern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Chief Administrator to the Minister of Education and Administrator of Southern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 府公彭成王義康專覽政事，不欲自下厝意。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang monopolized review of government affairs and did not wish to defer to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang monopolized policy review and would not defer to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 而登之性剛，每陳己志，義康不悅，出為吳郡太守，以贓貨免官。

translations.literal: But Dengzhi's nature was hard; he always stated his own views, and Yikang was displeased and sent him out as Administrator of Wu Commandery, then dismissed him from office for embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi was stiff-necked and always pressed his own views; Yikang, displeased, posted him to Wu Commandery and later dismissed him for graft.

sentences.zh: 後拜豫章太守，徵為中護軍，未拜卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Yuzhang, summoned as General Who Protects the Army, and died before taking up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Administrator of Yuzhang and summoned as General Who Protects the Army, but died before accepting.

sentences.zh: 仲文位廣平太守，兄登之為謝晦長史，仲文往省之。

translations.literal: Zhongwen held the post of Administrator of Guangping; his elder brother Dengzhi was Chief Administrator to Xie Hui, and Zhongwen went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen was Administrator of Guangping; when his elder brother Dengzhi served Xie Hui as chief administrator, Zhongwen went to visit.

sentences.zh: 時晦權重，朝士並加敬，仲文獨與抗禮。

translations.literal: At that time Hui's power was heavy and court gentlemen all showed extra respect; only Zhongwen treated him as an equal.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's power was immense and courtiers bowed low; Zhongwen alone treated him as an equal.

sentences.zh: 後為彭城王義康驃騎主簿，未就，徙為丹陽丞。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Clerk to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang's Rapid Cavalry staff; before taking up the post he was transferred to Assistant Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later became chief clerk on Prince of Pengcheng Yikang's Rapid Cavalry staff; before reporting he was reassigned Assistant Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 既未到府，疑於府公禮敬，下禮官博議。

translations.literal: Having not yet reached the prince's office, he doubted the ceremonial respect owed the Prince, and submitted the question to the Masters of Rites for broad deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching the prince's office he questioned the ceremonial deference owed a prince and referred the matter to the Masters of Rites.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎裴松之議曰：「案春秋桓公八年，祭公逆王后于紀。

translations.literal: Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat Pei Songzhi argued: "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, eighth year of Duke Huan of Lu, Duke of Cai met the queen consort at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gentleman Pei Songzhi argued: "The Spring and Autumn Annals record that in Duke Huan's eighth year the Duke of Cai met the queen consort at Ji.

sentences.zh: 公羊傳曰：' 女在國稱女，此其稱王后何？

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says: 'A woman in her state is called "daughter"; why is she here called queen consort?
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary asks: 'At home she is called "daughter"—why here "queen consort"?

sentences.zh: 王者無外，其辭成矣。

translations.literal: The king has no outside—his wording is complete.'
translations.idiomatic: Because the king recognizes no outside, the title is complete.'"

sentences.zh: '推此而言，則仲文為吏之道，定於受敕之日矣。

translations.literal: Extending this, Zhongwen's path as an official was fixed from the day he received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: By that logic Zhongwen's duties as an official were fixed the day the edict reached him.

sentences.zh: 名器既正，則禮亦從之，安可未到廢其節乎？

translations.literal: Once name and office are correct, ritual follows accordingly—how can one before arrival discard one's propriety?
translations.idiomatic: Once title and office are settled, ritual follows—how can he abandon propriety before he even reports?

sentences.zh: 宜執吏禮。

translations.literal: He should observe the ritual of an official.
translations.idiomatic: He should observe an official's ritual.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Pei's view.

sentences.zh: 後始興王浚當鎮湘州，以仲文為司馬。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Shixing Jun was to be stationed at Xiang Province, Zhongwen was made Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shixing Jun was assigned to Xiang Province, Zhongwen was made his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 浚不之任，仍除南梁太守，司馬如故。

translations.literal: Jun did not take up the post; Zhongwen was instead appointed Administrator of Nanliang, retaining his post as Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jun never took the post; Zhongwen was instead appointed Administrator of Nanliang while keeping the chief administrator's title.

sentences.zh: 于時領軍劉湛協附大將軍彭城王義康，而與僕射殷景仁隙。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Guard General Liu Zhan attached himself to Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, while he had a rift with Vice Director Yin Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Guard General Liu Zhan clung to Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang while feuding with Vice Director Yin Jingren.

sentences.zh: 凡朝士游殷氏者，不得入劉氏之門，獨仲文遊二人間，密盡忠於朝廷。

translations.literal: Any court gentleman who visited the Yin household could not enter the Liu household; only Zhongwen moved between the two men and secretly gave full loyalty to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers who visited the Yin household were barred from Liu's gate; only Zhongwen moved between both camps and secretly served the throne.

sentences.zh: 景仁稱疾不朝見者歷年，文帝常令仲文銜命去來，湛不疑也。

translations.literal: Jingren claimed illness and did not attend court for years; Emperor Wen often had Zhongwen carry orders back and forth, and Zhan did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren feigned illness and stayed away from court for years; Emperor Wen used Zhongwen as courier, and Zhan suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 義康出蕃，湛伏誅，以仲文為尚書吏部郎，與右衛將軍沈演之俱參機密。

translations.literal: When Yikang went out to his fief and Zhan was executed, Zhongwen was made Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel and, with General of the Right Guard Shen Yanzhi, jointly handled secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang left for his fief and Zhan was executed, Zhongwen became Director of Personnel in the Masters of Writing and, with General of the Right Guard Shen Yanzhi, shared confidential state business.

sentences.zh: 曆侍中、吏部尚書，領義陽王師。

translations.literal: He successively served as Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently Tutor to Prince of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing to concurrent Tutor to Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 內外歸附，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: Inside and outside court submitted to him; his power tilted court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike rallied to him; his influence overshadowed the realm.

sentences.zh: 仲文為人強急不耐煩，賓客訴非理者，忿罵形於辭色。

translations.literal: Zhongwen as a man was forceful and impatient, unable to bear annoyance; when guests pleaded unreasonable cases, anger and scolding showed in his words and face.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen was forceful and short-tempered; when petitioners pressed unreasonable cases, rage showed plainly on his face and in his words.

sentences.zh: 素無術學，不為眾望所推。

translations.literal: He had never possessed learning in the arts and was not pushed forward by public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked scholarly training and enjoyed little esteem among the learned.

sentences.zh: 性好潔，士大夫造之者，未出戶輒令人拭席洗床。

translations.literal: By nature he loved cleanliness; when gentlemen visited him, before they had left the door he would have someone wipe the mat and wash the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Fastidious by nature, he had mats wiped and beds washed the moment a guest stepped out.

sentences.zh: 時陳郡殷沖亦好淨，小史非淨浴新衣，不得近左右，士大夫小不整潔，每容接之。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Chong of Chen Commandery also loved cleanliness; junior clerks who had not bathed and put on new clothes could not approach his side; if gentlemen were slightly untidy he still received them.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong of Chen Commandery was equally fastidious, yet he still received slightly unkempt gentlemen; his clerks, however, had to bathe and don fresh clothes before approaching.

sentences.zh: 仲文好潔反是，每以此見譏。

translations.literal: Zhongwen's love of cleanliness was the opposite; he was often mocked for this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's cleanliness ran the other way, and he was often ridiculed for it.

sentences.zh: 領選既不緝眾論，又頗通貨賄，用少府卿劉道錫為廣州刺史，道錫至鎮，餉白檀牽車，常自乘焉。

translations.literal: Overseeing selection he neither reconciled public opinion nor avoided trafficking in bribes; he appointed Director of the Palace Store Liu Daoxi Inspector of Guang Province, and when Daoxi reached his post he sent a white sandalwood carriage, which he always rode himself.
translations.idiomatic: As head of appointments he neither soothed opinion nor shunned bribes; he made Palace Store Director Liu Daoxi Inspector of Guang Province, and Daoxi sent him a white sandalwood carriage which he rode daily.

sentences.zh: 或以白文帝，帝見問曰：「道錫餉卿小車，裝飾甚麗，有之乎？

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Emperor Wen; the Emperor questioned him: "Did Daoxi send you a small carriage, very beautifully decorated—did you have such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed Emperor Wen, who asked, "Did Daoxi give you a small carriage, lavishly decorated—true or not?"

sentences.zh: 」仲文懼起謝。

translations.literal: Zhongwen in fear rose and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhongwen rose and apologized.

sentences.zh: 又仲文請急還家，吏部令史錢泰、主客令史周伯齊出仲文宅諮事。

translations.literal: Also Zhongwen requested urgent leave to return home; Personnel Director's clerks Qian Tai and Reception Director's clerk Zhou Boqi went to Zhongwen's residence to consult on business.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen also took emergency leave home; Personnel clerk Qian Tai and Reception clerk Zhou Boqi visited his house on official business.

sentences.zh: 泰能彈琵琶，伯齊善歌，仲文因留停宿。

translations.literal: Tai could play the pipa and Boqi was skilled at song; Zhongwen therefore kept them overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Tai played the pipa and Boqi sang well; Zhongwen kept them overnight.

sentences.zh: 尚書制，令史諮事不得宿停外，雖八座命亦不許，為有司所奏。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing regulations: clerks consulting on business must not lodge outside—even on the Eight Ministers' orders it was not permitted; he was reported by the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations forbade clerks from lodging outside while on business—even an Eight Minister's order could not override that; the responsible office reported him.

sentences.zh: 上于仲文素厚，將恕之，召問尚書右僕射何尚之，具陳仲文得失，奏言：

translations.literal: The Emperor had long favored Zhongwen and was about to pardon him; he summoned and questioned Vice Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi, who fully set forth Zhongwen's merits and faults and memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long favored Zhongwen and meant to forgive him, but summoned Vice Director He Shangzhi, who laid out Zhongwen's faults and merits in full:

sentences.zh: 仲文事如丘山，若縱而不糾，復何以為政。

translations.literal: Zhongwen's affairs are like hills; if indulged without correction, how can government proceed?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's offenses pile like hills; if indulged, how can government stand?

sentences.zh: 晉武不為明主，斷鬲令事，遂能奮發，華廙見待不輕，廢錮累年，後起改作城門校尉耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin was no enlightened ruler, yet on the matter of cutting off Ge Ling he was able to act decisively; Hua Mi was treated not lightly, yet was confined for years and later restored only as Colonel of the City Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin was no sage, yet he acted decisively against Ge Ling; Hua Mi enjoyed favor yet was confined for years and restored only as Colonel of the City Gate.

sentences.zh: 若言仲文有誠于國，未知的是何事，政當云與殷景仁不失其舊，與劉湛亦復不疏。

translations.literal: If one says Zhongwen has loyalty to the state, it is unclear what that loyalty consists in—it comes down to saying he has not broken with Yin Jingren and is not distant from Liu Zhan either.
translations.idiomatic: If one calls Zhongwen loyal, to what deed? At best he kept terms with Yin Jingren and did not break with Liu Zhan.

sentences.zh: 且景仁當時意事，豈復可蔑，縱有微誠，復何足掩其惡。

translations.literal: Moreover Jingren's designs at the time—can they be dismissed? Even if there were slight loyalty, how could it cover his wickedness?
translations.idiomatic: And can Jingren's designs be dismissed? Even minor loyalty cannot cover such wickedness.

sentences.zh: 賈充勳烈，晉之重臣，雖事業不稱，不聞有大罪，諸臣進說，便即遠出。

translations.literal: Jia Chong had meritorious achievement and was a heavy minister of Jin; though his career did not match his rank, no great crime was heard of—yet when ministers urged action he was immediately sent far away.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong was a meritorious pillar of Jin; though his career fell short of his rank, no grave crime was charged—yet ministers urged exile and he was sent away at once.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖叡，反更遲遲於此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sage and perspicacious, yet you delay all the more on this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sage and clear-sighted—yet you hesitate here.

sentences.zh: 仲文身上之釁，既自過於范曄，所少賊一事耳。

translations.literal: The offenses on Zhongwen's person already exceed Fan Ye's; he lacks only the single matter of treason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's personal offenses already exceed Fan Ye's; only outright treason is missing.

sentences.zh: 伏願深加三思。

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to reflect deeply three times.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this three times over.

sentences.zh: 試以諸聲傳普訪諸可顧問者，群下見陛下顧遇既重，恐不敢苦侵傷，顧問之日，宜布嫌責之旨。

translations.literal: Try spreading word among all who can be consulted; when the multitude sees Your Majesty's favor is heavy, they will fear to wound him severely—on the day of consultation you should announce intent to blame and reprove.
translations.idiomatic: Sound out every adviser you trust; seeing Your Majesty's favor, they will fear to wound him—on consultation day announce blame in advance.

sentences.zh: 若不如此，亦當不辨有所得失。

translations.literal: If not so, they likewise will not distinguish gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they will not speak plainly of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 時仲文自理不諳台制，令史並言停外非嫌。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongwen argued in his own defense that he did not understand Secretariat regulations; the clerks all said lodging outside was no offense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen pleaded ignorance of Secretariat rules; the clerks claimed overnight lodging was no crime.

sentences.zh: 帝以小事不足傷大臣，尚之又陳：

translations.literal: The Emperor considered it a small matter unworthy of harming a great minister; Shangzhi again stated:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought it too small to harm a great minister; Shangzhi pressed again:

sentences.zh: 令史具向仲文說不得停之意，仲文了不聽納，非為不解，直是苟相留耳。

translations.literal: The clerks fully explained to Zhongwen the reason lodging was forbidden; Zhongwen utterly refused to accept—not that he did not understand, but simply insisted on keeping them.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks explained the ban to Zhongwen; he refused outright—not from ignorance but from wilful retention.

sentences.zh: 雖是令史出，乃遠虧朝典，又不得謂之小事。

translations.literal: Though it was clerks who went out, it deeply violated court precedent and cannot be called a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Though only clerks were involved, the breach of court precedent was grave—not a trifle.

sentences.zh: 謝晦望實非今者之疇，一事錯誤，免侍中官。

translations.literal: Xie Hui's reputation and substance are not of today's class; one error cost him his Palace Attendant's post.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui's standing was not of today's rank; one mistake cost him the Palace Attendant's post.

sentences.zh: 王珣時賢少失，桓胤春搜之謬，皆白衣領職，況公犯憲制邪？

translations.literal: Wang Xun's youthful slip, Huan Yin's error at the spring hunt—all served in plain clothes while retaining office; how much more when one violates statutory regulations?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun's youthful fault and Huan Yin's spring-hunt blunder both brought service in plain clothes while keeping office—how much more when one violates statute?

sentences.zh: 孔萬祀居左局，言：「仲文貴要異他尚書」。

translations.literal: Kong Wansi's post in the Left Bureau said: "Zhongwen's nobility and importance differ from other Directors."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wansi in the Left Bureau said, "Zhongwen's rank and power differ from other directors."

sentences.zh: 又云：「不癡不聾，不成姑公」。

translations.literal: He also said: "Without deafness or foolishness one cannot be a mother-in-law or father-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Only the deaf and foolish make good in-laws."

sentences.zh: 敢作此言，亦為異也。

translations.literal: To dare such words is also strange.
translations.idiomatic: To speak so boldly was itself extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 文帝猶優遊，使尚之更陳其意。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen still lingered in deliberation and had Shangzhi state his meaning again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen still wavered and asked Shangzhi to speak again.

sentences.zh: 尚之備言仲文愆曰：

translations.literal: Shangzhi fully set forth Zhongwen's faults:
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi laid out Zhongwen's faults in full:

sentences.zh: 臣思張遼之言，關羽雖兄弟，曹公父子豈得不言。

translations.literal: Your servant recalls Zhang Liao's words: though Guan Yu was like a brother, how could Lord Cao and his son fail to speak?
translations.idiomatic: I recall Zhang Liao: though Guan Yu was as a brother, could Cao Cao and his son stay silent?

sentences.zh: 觀今人臣憂國甚寡，臣復結舌，日月之明或有所蔽。

translations.literal: Observing ministers today, few worry for the state; if your servant again holds his tongue, even the sun and moon may have blind spots.
translations.idiomatic: Few ministers today worry for the state; if I hold my tongue, even sun and moon may have blind spots.

sentences.zh: 然不知臣者豈不謂臣有爭競之心，亦追以悵悵。

translations.literal: Yet those who do not know your servant will surely say he has a contentious heart; I too am troubled with regret.
translations.idiomatic: Those who do not know me will call me contentious; I am troubled and regretful.

sentences.zh: 臣與仲文周旋，俱被恩接，不宜復生厚薄。

translations.literal: Your servant and Zhongwen have moved in company, both receiving grace and access; one should not again produce favor and coldness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen and I both enjoyed imperial favor; I should not now show partiality.

sentences.zh: 太尉昨與臣言說仲文有諸不可，非唯一條，遠近相崇畏，震動四海。

translations.literal: Yesterday the Grand Commandant spoke with your servant of Zhongwen's many improprieties—not only one item; near and far alike revere and fear him, shaking the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the Grand Commandant told me of Zhongwen's many improprieties—not one alone; near and far revere and fear him, shaking the realm.

sentences.zh: 仲文先與劉德願殊惡，德願自持琵琶甚精麗遺之，便復款然。

translations.literal: Zhongwen had formerly been on very bad terms with Liu Deyuan; Deyuan sent him a very fine pipa he kept himself, and at once they were on intimate terms again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen once despised Liu Deyuan; Deyuan sent his own exquisite pipa and intimacy returned at once.

sentences.zh: 市令盛馥進數百口材助營宅，恐人知，作虛買券。

translations.literal: Market magistrate Sheng Fu presented several hundred beams of timber to help build his residence; fearing people would know, he made false purchase vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: Market magistrate Sheng Fu sent hundreds of beams for his house; fearing exposure, he forged purchase receipts.

sentences.zh: 劉道錫驟有所輸，傾南奉之半。

translations.literal: Liu Daoxi suddenly made gifts; he poured out half of the southern tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoxi showered him with gifts, draining half the southern tribute.

sentences.zh: 劉雍自謂得其力助，事之如父，夏中送甘蔗，若新發於州。

translations.literal: Liu Yong considered himself aided by Zhongwen's power and served him like a father; in midsummer he sent sugarcane as if freshly dispatched from the province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong, thinking himself backed by Zhongwen, served him like a father and sent midsummer sugarcane as if fresh from the province.

sentences.zh: 國吏運載櫵蘇，無輟於道。

translations.literal: Provincial clerks transporting firewood and kindling on the roads never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial clerks hauling firewood never left the roads.

sentences.zh: 諸見人有物，鮮或不求，聞劉遵考有材便乞材，見好燭盤便復乞之。

translations.literal: Of anyone he saw who had goods, few escaped without a request; hearing Liu Zunkao had timber he begged timber; seeing a fine candle stand he begged that too.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever had goods rarely escaped his demands; hearing Liu Zunkao had timber he begged timber; seeing a fine candle stand he begged that too.

sentences.zh: 選用不平，不可一二。

translations.literal: Unfairness in selection cannot be counted on one or two fingers.
translations.idiomatic: Unfair appointments were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 太尉又言仲文都無共事之體，凡所選舉悉是其意，政令太尉知耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant also said Zhongwen entirely lacked the bearing of one who shares office; all selections were his will alone—the Grand Commandant was informed only in name.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant said Zhongwen would not share power; every appointment was his alone—the Grand Commandant learned of them in name only.

sentences.zh: 論虞秀之作黃門，太尉不正答和，故得停。

translations.literal: On discussing Yu Xiu's appointment as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, the Grand Commandant did not properly respond in agreement, and so the appointment was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Xiu was proposed for Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, the Grand Commandant withheld assent and the appointment stalled.

sentences.zh: 太尉近與仲文疏，欲用德願兒作州西曹，仲文乃啟用為主簿，即語德願以謝太尉。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant had recently grown distant from Zhongwen and wished to use Deyuan's son as Western Staff Officer of the province; Zhongwen instead memorialized appointing him Chief Clerk and told Deyuan to thank the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant, lately estranged, wanted Deyuan's son as provincial western staff officer; Zhongwen appointed him chief clerk instead and told Deyuan to thank the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 前後漏泄賣恩，亦復何極。

translations.literal: Leaking secrets and selling favors before and after—again, to what limit?
translations.idiomatic: Leaking secrets and trading favors—where was the limit?

sentences.zh: 縱不罪，故宜出之。

translations.literal: Even if not punished, he should still be sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Even without punishment he should be removed.

sentences.zh: 自從裴、劉刑罰已來，諸將陳力百倍，今日事實好惡可問，若赫然發憤，顯明法憲，陛下便可閑臥紫闥無復一事也。

translations.literal: Since the punishments of Pei and Liu, the generals have exerted strength a hundredfold; today's facts of good and evil can be asked—if Your Majesty suddenly shows anger and makes the law manifest, Your Majesty can lie at ease in the Purple Hall with nothing further to do.
translations.idiomatic: Since Pei and Liu were punished the generals have exerted themselves a hundredfold; the facts of good and evil can be asked—if Your Majesty acts in wrath and makes law visible, you may rest in the Purple Hall with nothing left to do.

sentences.zh: 帝欲出仲文為丹陽，又以問尚之，答言：

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to send Zhongwen out as Intendant of Danyang and again questioned Shangzhi, who answered:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to post Zhongwen as Intendant of Danyang and asked Shangzhi again; he answered:

sentences.zh: 仲文蹈罪負恩，陛下遲遲舊恩，未忍窮法，方復有尹京赫赫之授。

translations.literal: Zhongwen treads on crime and bears ingratitude; Your Majesty delays out of old favor and will not exhaust the law, yet would again grant the illustrious appointment of governing the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen has offended and betrayed favor; Your Majesty, clinging to old kindness, would not exhaust the law—yet would give him the capital intendant's glittering post.

sentences.zh: 恐悉心奉國之人於此而息，貪狼恣意，歲月滋甚。

translations.literal: I fear those who devote themselves to serving the state will cease here; the greedy and wolfish will grow bolder month by month.
translations.idiomatic: Men who serve the state wholeheartedly will fall silent; the greedy and ruthless will grow bolder by the month.

sentences.zh: 如臣所聞天下議論，仲文恒塵累日月，未見一毫增輝，乃更成形勢，是老王雅也。

translations.literal: As your servant hears the talk under heaven, Zhongwen constantly dims the sun and moon without adding a hair's breadth of luster; yet he forms power all the more—this is old Wang Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Public talk says Zhongwen only dims the sun and moon without adding a glimmer of light—yet grows more powerful; he is another Wang Ya.

sentences.zh: 古人言，無賞罰，雖堯舜不能為政。

translations.literal: The ancients said: without reward and punishment, even Yao and Shun cannot govern.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: without reward and punishment even Yao and Shun cannot govern.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈可坐損皇家之重，迷一凡人。

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty sit and damage the weight of the imperial house, bewildered by one ordinary man?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty sit and weaken the imperial house, bewitched by one ordinary man?

sentences.zh: 令賈誼、劉向重生，豈不慷慨流涕於聖世邪。

translations.literal: If Jia Yi and Liu Xiang were reborn, would they not pour forth passionate tears in this sage age?
translations.idiomatic: Were Jia Yi and Liu Xiang reborn, would they not weep in this enlightened age?

sentences.zh: 臣昔啟范曄，當時亦懼犯觸之尤，苟是愚懷所挹，政自不能不舒達，所謂「雖九死而不悔。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly memorialized on Fan Ye; at that time too he feared the utmost of offense; if it was what his foolish heart held, he could not but express it—the so-called "though nine deaths he would not regret."
translations.idiomatic: I once memorialized on Fan Ye, fearing grave offense; what my foolish heart held I had to speak—the saying, "though nine deaths I would not regret."

translations.literal: Thus.
translations.idiomatic: So I spoke.

sentences.zh: 臣謂仲文且外出，若能修改，在職著稱，還亦不難，而得少明國典，粗酬四海之誚。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that Zhongwen should for the time go outside; if he can reform and in office achieve reputation, return is not difficult, and the state's laws will be somewhat clarified, roughly answering the reproach of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Send Zhongwen out for now; if he reforms and earns reputation in office, recall is easy—and the state's laws will be partly clarified, answering public reproach.

sentences.zh: 今愆釁如山，榮任不損，仲文若復有彰大之罪，誰敢以聞。

translations.literal: Now faults like mountains, honor and office undiminished—if Zhongwen again commits a glaring great crime, who will dare report it?
translations.idiomatic: Faults pile like mountains yet honor stands untouched—if Zhongwen commits another glaring crime, who will dare report it?

sentences.zh: 亦知陛下不能采臣之言，故是臣不能以己之意耳。

translations.literal: I also know Your Majesty cannot adopt your servant's words; therefore your servant cannot act by his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: I know Your Majesty will not take my counsel; therefore I cannot act on my own judgment.

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He added:

sentences.zh: 臣見劉伯龍大慷慨仲文所行，言有人送張幼緒，語人「吾雖得一縣，負錢三十萬。

translations.literal: Your servant saw Liu Bolong greatly indignant at Zhongwen's conduct, saying someone sent Zhang Youxu, telling people: "Though I got one county, I owe three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bolong was furious at Zhongwen's conduct, saying someone sent Zhang Youxu with the remark, "I got one county but owe three hundred thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 庾仲遠仍當送至新林，見縛束猶未得解手」。

translations.literal: Yu Zhongyuan will still have to deliver him to Xinlin; seeing him bound he still cannot free his hands."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongyuan will haul him to Xinlin bound hand and foot before he can breathe free."

sentences.zh: 荀萬秋嘗詣仲文，逢一客姓夏侯，主人問：「有好牛不？

translations.literal: Xun Wanqiu once visited Zhongwen and met a guest surnamed Xiahou; the host asked: "Do you have a good ox?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun Wanqiu once visited Zhongwen and met a guest named Xiahou; the host asked, "Any good ox?"

sentences.zh: 」言無。

translations.literal: He said there was none.
translations.idiomatic: The guest said no.

sentences.zh: 問：「有好馬不？

translations.literal: He asked: "Do you have a good horse?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "Any good horse?"

sentences.zh: 」又言無，政有佳驢耳。

translations.literal: Again he said there was none; he had only a fine donkey.
translations.idiomatic: Again no—only a fine donkey.

sentences.zh: 仲文便答：「甚是所欲。

translations.literal: Zhongwen at once answered: "That is exactly what is desired."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen instantly said, "That is precisely what I want."

sentences.zh: 」客出門。

translations.literal: The guest went out the door.
translations.idiomatic: The guest left.

sentences.zh: 遂相聞索之。

translations.literal: Thereupon word was sent asking for it.
translations.idiomatic: Word was sent at once demanding the donkey.

sentences.zh: 劉道錫言是仲文所舉，就道錫索嫁女具及祠器，乃當百萬數，猶謂不然。

translations.literal: Liu Daoxi said it was Zhongwen's recommendation; he went to Daoxi demanding bridal dowry goods and sacrificial vessels—amounting to a million, and still considered it insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoxi said Zhongwen had recommended him; Zhongwen then demanded bridal dowry and sacrificial vessels from Daoxi worth a million—and still called it too little.

sentences.zh: 選令史章龍向臣說，亦歎其受納之過。

translations.literal: Selection clerk Zhang Long told your servant and also sighed at the excess of his acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Selection clerk Zhang Long told me and sighed at the scale of his takings.

sentences.zh: 言實得嫁女銅爐，四人舉乃勝，細葛鬥帳等物不可稱數。

translations.literal: He said he truly received a bridal copper brazier requiring four men to lift, fine-ge summer canopy curtains and the like in untold numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He truly took a bridal copper brazier needing four men to lift, fine-ge summer canopies, and countless like items.

sentences.zh: 在尚書中令奴酤酃酒，利其百十，亦是立台閣所無，不審少簡聖聽不？

translations.literal: While in the Masters of Writing he had a slave sell Ling wine and profited a hundred or ten—this too is unheard of in establishing the Secretariat; I do not know whether it slightly reached the sage's ear?
translations.idiomatic: In the Masters of Writing he had a slave sell Ling wine for petty profit—unheard of in the Secretariat; I do not know whether this reached Your Majesty's ear?

sentences.zh: 帝乃可有司之奏，免仲文官，卒于家。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon approved the responsible office's memorial, dismissed Zhongwen from office, and he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial, dismissed Zhongwen, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: 帝錄其宿誠，追贈本官。

translations.literal: The Emperor recorded his old loyalty and posthumously restored his original office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted his earlier loyalty and posthumously restored his rank.

sentences.zh: 子弘遠。

translations.literal: His son Hongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongyuan.

sentences.zh: 弘遠字士操，清實有士譽。

translations.literal: Hongyuan, courtesy name Shicao, was pure and solid and enjoyed reputation among gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan, styled Shicao, was upright and solid and enjoyed esteem among gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為江州長史。

translations.literal: Serving Qi he was Chief Administrator of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as Chief Administrator of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 刺史陳顯達舉兵敗，斬於朱雀航。

translations.literal: Inspector Chen Xianda raised troops and was defeated; he was beheaded at Zhuque Crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Chen Xianda rebelled and was defeated, Hongyuan was beheaded at Zhuque Crossing.

sentences.zh: 將刑，索帽著之，曰：「子路結纓，吾不可以不冠而死。

translations.literal: About to be executed, he asked for a cap and put it on, saying: "Zilu tied his cap— I cannot die without a cap."
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution he asked for a cap, saying, "Zilu tied his cap before death—I cannot die bareheaded."

sentences.zh: 」謂看者曰：「吾非賊，乃是義兵，為諸君請命耳。

translations.literal: He said to onlookers: "I am no rebel but righteous troops, pleading life for you all."
translations.idiomatic: He told the crowd, "I am no rebel but a man of righteous arms, pleading for your lives."

sentences.zh: 陳公太輕事，若用吾言，天下將免塗炭。

translations.literal: Lord Chen took the matter too lightly; had he used my words, the realm would have been spared scorched earth.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Chen treated the affair too lightly; had he heeded me, the realm would have been spared ruin.

sentences.zh: 」弘遠子子曜年十四，抱持父乞代命，遂並殺之。

translations.literal: Hongyuan's son Ziyao, age fourteen, embraced his father begging to die in his stead; they were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan's fourteen-year-old son Ziyao clung to his father begging to die in his place; both were killed.

sentences.zh: 仲文從弟徽之位御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zhongwen's clansman younger brother Huizhi held the post of Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's clansman Huizhi served as Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 徽之子漪，齊邵陵王記室。

translations.literal: Huizhi's son Yi was Recorder to Prince of Shaoling of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi's son Yi was recorder to Prince of Shaoling of Qi.

sentences.zh: 漪子仲容。

translations.literal: Yi's son Zhongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Zhongrong.

sentences.zh: 仲容字子仲，幼孤，為叔父泳所養。

translations.literal: Zhongrong, courtesy name Zizhong, was orphaned young and was raised by his uncle Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong, styled Zizhong, lost his father young and was raised by his uncle Yong.

sentences.zh: 及長，杜絕人事，專精篤學，晝夜手不輟卷。

translations.literal: When grown he cut off worldly affairs, devoted himself to earnest study, and day and night his hand did not leave the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he withdrew from worldly affairs and studied relentlessly, never setting book aside day or night.

sentences.zh: 初為安西法曹行參軍，泳時貴顯，吏部尚書徐勉擬泳子晏嬰為宮僚。

translations.literal: He first became Acting Adjutant in the Law Section of the Pacifying West Army; Yong was then noble and prominent, and Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Mian planned Yong's son Yan'ying as palace staff.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as acting adjutant in the Pacifying West Army's law section; his uncle Yong was then powerful, and Director Xu Mian planned Yong's son Yan'ying for palace staff.

sentences.zh: 泳泣曰：「兄子幼孤，人才粗可，願以晏嬰所忝回用之。

translations.literal: Yong wept and said: "My elder brother's son is orphaned young; his talent is roughly adequate—I wish to transfer what Yan'ying would receive to him."
translations.idiomatic: Yong wept and said, "My brother's orphaned son has passable talent—give Yan'ying's post to him instead."

sentences.zh: 」勉許焉。

translations.literal: Mian consented.
translations.idiomatic: Mian agreed.

sentences.zh: 轉仲容為太子舍人，遷安成王主簿。

translations.literal: Zhongrong was transferred to Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent and promoted to Chief Clerk to Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong was transferred to Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent and promoted Chief Clerk to Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 時平原劉峻亦為府佐，並以強學為王所禮接。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Jun of Pingyuan was also a staff officer; both were treated with ceremony by the prince for their forceful learning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun of Pingyuan was also on the prince's staff; both were honored for formidable scholarship.

sentences.zh: 後為永康、錢唐、武康令，並無績，多被推劾。

translations.literal: Later he was magistrate of Yongkang, Qiantang, and Wukang—all without achievement and often impeached.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Yongkang, Qiantang, and Wukang—without distinction and often impeached.

sentences.zh: 久之，除安成王中記室。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Recorder to Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was appointed recorder to Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 當出隨府，皇太子以舊恩降餞，賜詩曰：「孫生陟陽道，吳子朝歌縣，未若樊林舉，置酒臨華殿。

translations.literal: When about to go out following the prince's transfer, the Crown Prince, out of old favor, descended to send him off and bestowed a poem: "Master Sun climbs the road to Yang, Master Wu the county of Chaoge—nothing like Fan Lin's rise, setting wine before the splendid hall."
translations.idiomatic: When he was to follow the prince's transfer, the crown prince, remembering old favor, came down to farewell him with a poem: "Master Sun climbs Yang's road, Master Wu governs Chaoge—none like Fan Lin's ascent, feasting before the splendid hall."

sentences.zh: 」時輩榮之。

translations.literal: Men of the age honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左丞，坐推糾不直免官。

translations.literal: Later he was Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and was dismissed from office for impeachment that was not upright.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and was dismissed when his impeachments proved unfair.

sentences.zh: 仲容博學，少有盛名，頗任氣使酒，好危言高論，士友以此少之。

translations.literal: Zhongrong was broadly learned and from youth had great fame; he was rather willful with wine, loved startling words and lofty discourse, and gentlemen for this thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong was widely learned and famous early; willful with wine, he loved shocking pronouncements, and gentlemen thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 唯與王籍、謝幾卿情好相得，二人時亦不調，遂相追隨，誕縱酣飲，不持檢操。

translations.literal: Only with Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing was he close in feeling; the two at the time were also unrestrained, and so they followed one another, indulging in wild drinking without holding to propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing were true friends; both were unrestrained, and together they drank wildly without restraint.

sentences.zh: 遇太清亂，遊會稽卒。

translations.literal: He met the chaos of the Taiping era, wandered to Kuaiji, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived through the Taiping turmoil, wandered to Kuaiji, and died there.

sentences.zh: 仲容抄子書三十卷，諸集三十卷，眾家地理書二十卷，列女傳三卷，文集二十卷，並行於代。

translations.literal: Zhongrong copied thirty juan of miscellaneous masters' works, thirty juan of various collections, twenty juan of geographical works of many schools, three juan of Biographies of Exemplary Women, and twenty juan of collected writings—all circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong compiled thirty juan of miscellany, thirty of collected writings, twenty of geography, three of Exemplary Women, and twenty of his own prose—all circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 顧琛字弘瑋，吳郡吳人，晉司空和之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Gu Chen, courtesy name Hongwei, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery, great-grandson of Jin Minister of Works Gu Hezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen, styled Hongwei, came from Wu in Wu Commandery and was great-grandson of Jin Minister of Works Gu Hezhi.

sentences.zh: 祖履之，父惔，並為司徒左西曹掾。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lüzhi and father Tan both served as Aides in the Left and Right Western Sections of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lüzhi and father Tan both served as aides in the Minister of Education's western sections.

sentences.zh: 琛謹確不尚浮華，起家州從事、駙馬都尉，累遷尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: Chen was careful and solid and did not esteem flashy display; he began his career as Provincial Aide and Commandant of the Horse Consorts, and was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman in the Arsenal Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was careful and unflashy; he began as provincial aide and Commandant of the Horse Consorts and rose to Gentleman in the Arsenal Section.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年，文帝遣到彥之經略河南，大敗，悉委棄兵甲，武庫為之空虛。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia, Emperor Wen sent Dao Yanzhi to plan Henan; he was greatly defeated, abandoned all armor and weapons, and the arsenal was emptied by it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia's seventh year Emperor Wen sent Dao Yanzhi to recover Henan; the army was routed, armor and weapons were abandoned, and the arsenal lay empty.

sentences.zh: 文帝宴會，有歸化人在座，上問琛庫中仗猶有幾許？

translations.literal: At an imperial banquet a surrendered foreigner was seated; the Emperor asked Chen how many weapons remained in the arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet a surrendered foreigner was present; the emperor asked Chen how many weapons the arsenal still held.

sentences.zh: 琛詭辭答有十萬人仗。

translations.literal: Chen evasively answered that there were arms for a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Chen evasively answered arms enough for a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 舊庫仗秘不言多少，上既發問，追悔失言。

translations.literal: By old custom the arsenal's arms were secret and the number was not spoken; the Emperor having asked regretted his slip of tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Arsenal stores were secret by custom; having asked, the emperor regretted his slip.

sentences.zh: 及琛詭對，上甚善之。

translations.literal: When Chen answered evasively the Emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's evasive answer pleased the emperor greatly.

sentences.zh: 尚書寺門有制，八坐以下門生隨入者各有差，不得雜以人士。

translations.literal: At the Masters of Writing temple gate there was a regulation: below the Eight Ministers, retainers entering with their lords each had fixed quotas and might not mix in outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations at the Masters of Writing gate fixed retainer quotas for ranks below the Eight Ministers and forbade outsiders.

sentences.zh: 琛以宗人顧碩寄尚書張茂度門名，而與顧碩同席坐。

translations.literal: Chen had his clansman Gu Shuo registered under Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Maodu's retainer name and sat at the same mat with Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Chen registered clansman Gu Shuo under Director Zhang Maodu's retainer list and sat with him on the same mat.

sentences.zh: 明年坐譴出，免中正。

translations.literal: The next year he was punished by reprimand and dismissal and was removed as Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was reprimanded and dismissed and lost his post as Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 凡尚書官大罪則免，小罪譴出，譴出者百日無代人，聽還本職。

translations.literal: Generally Masters of Writing officials for great crime were dismissed, for small crime reprimanded and sent out; those sent out had no replacement for a hundred days and were then permitted to return to original office.
translations.idiomatic: Great crimes brought dismissal; lesser ones reprimand and temporary removal—after a hundred days without replacement one could return.

sentences.zh: 琛仍為彭城王義康所請，再補司徒錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Chen was again requested by Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and again supplemented as Recording Secretary to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang recalled him as Recording Secretary to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 十五年，出為義興太守。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he went out as Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 初，義康請琛入府，欲委以腹心，琛不能承事劉湛，故尋見斥外。

translations.literal: Earlier Yikang had requested Chen enter his staff, wishing to entrust him as confidant; Chen could not serve under Liu Zhan and so was soon expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang had wanted Chen as confidant, but Chen would not serve under Liu Zhan and was soon pushed out.

sentences.zh: 十九年，徙東陽太守，欲使琛防守彭城王義康，固辭忤旨，廢黜還家積年。
