translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred Administrator of Dongyang, intending that Chen guard Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; he firmly declined against the imperial will and was dismissed and sent home for many years.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was moved to Dongyang to guard Yikang; he refused against the emperor's will and was dismissed for years.

sentences.zh: 及元凶弑立，分會稽五郡置州，以隨王誕為刺史，即以琛為會稽太守。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince usurped and established himself, five commanderies of Kuaiji were separated to form a province; Prince of Sui Wang Dan was made Inspector and Chen was made Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince usurped the throne, five Kuaiji commanderies became a province under Prince of Sui Wang Dan; Chen became Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 誕起義，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Dan raised righteous troops he was promoted General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan raised righteous arms he was promoted General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was transferred Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was settled he became Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，為吳郡太守，以起義功，封永新縣五等侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian he was Administrator of Wu Commandery; for merit in the righteous rising he was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Yongxin County.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian's first year he governed Wu Commandery; for the righteous rising he was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，吳縣令張闓坐居母喪無禮，下廷尉，錢唐令沈文秀判劾違謬，應坐被彈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, Magistrate of Wu County Zhang Kan sat in mourning for his mother without propriety and was sent to the Court of Justice; Magistrate of Qiantang Shen Wenxiu judged the impeachment erroneous and should himself have been impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming's first year Wu County magistrate Zhang Kan violated mourning propriety and was sent to trial; Qiantang magistrate Shen Wenxiu had judged wrongly and should himself have been impeached.

sentences.zh: 琛宣言於眾，「闓被劾之始，屢相申明」。

translations.literal: Chen declared to the multitude: "From the start of Kan's impeachment I repeatedly clarified the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Chen publicly declared, "From the start of Kan's impeachment I repeatedly clarified the matter."

sentences.zh: 又云：「當啟文秀留縣」。

translations.literal: He also said: "I shall memorialize to keep Wenxiu in the county."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "I shall memorialize to keep Wenxiu in office."

sentences.zh: 孝武聞之大怒，謂琛賣惡歸上，免官。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu heard and was greatly enraged, saying Chen was selling evil back to the throne, and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, hearing this, raged that Chen was shifting blame upward and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 琛母老仍停家。

translations.literal: Chen's mother was old and he remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's mother was elderly and he stayed home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 琛及前西陽太守張牧並事司空竟陵王誕，誕反，遣客陸延稔齎書板琛及子弟官。

translations.literal: Chen and former Administrator of Xiyang Zhang Mu both served Minister of Works Prince of Jingling Wang Dan; when Dan rebelled he sent his agent Lu Yanren bearing written commissions for Chen and his sons' offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and former Xiyang Administrator Zhang Mu both served Minister of Works Prince of Jingling Wang Dan; when Dan rebelled he sent Lu Yanren with commissions for Chen and his sons.

sentences.zh: 時孝武以琛素結事誕，或有異志，遣信就吳郡太守王曇生誅琛父子。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu, because Chen had long been tied to Dan and might harbor divergent intent, sent a messenger to Wu Commandery Administrator Wang Tansheng to execute Chen and his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, suspecting Chen's old ties to Dan, sent Wang Tansheng, Administrator of Wu Commandery, to execute Chen and his sons.

sentences.zh: 會延稔先至，琛等即執斬之，遣二子送延稔首啟聞。

translations.literal: It happened that Yanren arrived first; Chen and the others at once seized and beheaded him and sent two sons with Yanren's head to report.
translations.idiomatic: Yanren arrived first; Chen seized and beheaded him and sent two sons with the head to report.

sentences.zh: 孝武所遣誅琛使其日亦至而獲免。

translations.literal: The executioner Xiaowu had sent to kill Chen arrived the same day and Chen was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial execution party arrived the same day; Chen was spared.

sentences.zh: 琛母孔氏時年百餘歲，晉安帝隆安初，琅邪王廞于吳中作亂，以女為貞烈將軍，悉以女人為官屬，以孔氏為司馬。

translations.literal: Chen's mother Lady Kong was then over a hundred years old; at the beginning of Long'an under Emperor An of Jin, Prince of Langye Wang Yin made rebellion in Wu and made his daughter General of Chaste Martyrs, appointing all women as officials and making Lady Kong Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's mother Lady Kong was then over a hundred; at Jin Emperor An's Long'an era Prince of Langye Wang Yin rebelled in Wu, made his daughter General of Chaste Martyrs, staffed offices with women, and made Lady Kong chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 及孫恩亂後，東土饑荒，人相食，孔氏散家糧以振邑裏，得活者甚眾，生子皆以孔為名焉。

translations.literal: After Sun En's rebellion the eastern lands suffered famine and people ate one another; Lady Kong distributed household grain to relieve the district; those who lived were very many, and sons born were all given the name Kong.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun En's rebellion famine drove men to cannibalism; Lady Kong distributed grain through the district and saved many; grateful families named sons Kong.

sentences.zh: 琛仍為吳興太守，明年坐郡人多翦錢及盜鑄免官。

translations.literal: Chen again became Administrator of Wuxing; the next year he was dismissed for the commandery's widespread coin-clipping and illicit casting.
translations.idiomatic: Chen again governed Wuxing; the next year he was dismissed when the commandery clipped coins and cast illicit cash.

sentences.zh: 歷位都官尚書。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Director of the Masters of Writing for Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Director of Punishments in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Fei ascended he was Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Fei ascended he again governed Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，琛景平中為朝請，假還東，日晚至方山。

translations.literal: Earlier in the Jingping era Chen was Court Gentleman for Consultation and took leave to return east; he reached Fang Mountain late in the day.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Jingping era, Chen was Court Gentleman for Consultation returning east and reached Fang Mountain at dusk.

sentences.zh: 于時商旅數十船，悉泊岸側，有一人玄衣介幘，執鞭屏諸船云：「顧吳郡部伍尋至，應泊此岸。

translations.literal: At that time several dozen merchant boats all moored on the shore; a man in dark clothes with a kerchief cap held a whip and cleared the boats saying: "Gu the Administrator of Wu's retinue will soon arrive and should moor on this shore."
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of merchant boats lay at shore when a man in dark clothes and kerchief cap drove them off: "Gu, Administrator of Wu, approaches—moor here."

sentences.zh: 」於是諸船各東西。

translations.literal: Thereupon the boats each went east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The boats scattered east and west.

sentences.zh: 俄有一假裝至，事力甚寡，仍泊向處，人問：「顧吳郡早晚至？

translations.literal: Soon a modest boat arrived with very few attendants and still moored at the former place; people asked: "When will Gu the Administrator of Wu arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon a modest boat with few attendants moored where the others had been; people asked, "When does Gu, Administrator of Wu, arrive?"

sentences.zh: 」船人答：「無顧吳郡。

translations.literal: The boatmen answered: "There is no Gu the Administrator of Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The boatmen said, "There is no Administrator Gu."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「何船？

translations.literal: They asked again: "What boat is this?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked, "Whose boat then?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「顧朝請耳。

translations.literal: They said: "Only Gu the Court Gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Only Court Gentleman Gu."

sentences.zh: 」莫不驚怪。

translations.literal: None failed to be startled and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: All were astonished.

sentences.zh: 琛意竊知為善征，因誓之曰：「若得郡，當於此立廟。

translations.literal: Chen secretly knew it was a good omen and therefore vowed: "If I obtain the commandery I shall establish a temple here."
translations.idiomatic: Chen took it as a good omen and vowed, "If I win the commandery I shall build a temple here."

sentences.zh: 」至是果為吳郡，乃立廟方山，號白馬廟云。

translations.literal: At this he indeed became Administrator of Wu Commandery and thereupon established a temple at Fang Mountain, called the White Horse Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He did become Administrator of Wu and built the White Horse Temple at Fang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始初，與四方同反。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi under Emperor Ming he rebelled with the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Ming's Taishi opening he joined the four-direction rebellion.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，奉母奔會稽，台軍既至，歸降，後為員外常侍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: When troops were defeated he escorted his mother and fled to Kuaiji; when imperial troops arrived he surrendered and was later Extraordinary Palace Attendant and Palace Gentleman for Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he fled with his mother to Kuaiji, surrendered when imperial troops arrived, and later served as Extraordinary Palace Attendant and Gentleman for Regular Attendance.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 次子寶先，大明中，為尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: The second son Baoxian, in the Daming era, was Gentleman in the Water Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Baoxian, in the Daming era, was Gentleman in the Water Section.

sentences.zh: 先是，琛為左丞荀萬秋所劾，及寶先為郎，萬秋猶在職，自陳不拜。

translations.literal: Earlier Chen had been impeached by Left Assistant Director Xun Wanqiu; when Baoxian became Gentleman Wanqiu was still in office and declared he would not bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had once been impeached by Left Assistant Director Xun Wanqiu; when Baoxian took office Wanqiu still served and refused to bow to him.

sentences.zh: 孝武詔曰：「敕違糾慢，憲司之職，若有不公，自當更有厘改。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu edicted: "Disobeying orders and impeaching with negligence is the censorate's duty; if there is injustice there should naturally be further correction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered: "Disobedience and negligent impeachment are the censorate's concern; injustice should be corrected elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 而自頃劾無輕重，輒致私絕，此風難長，主者嚴為其科。

translations.literal: But recently impeachments without distinction of weight have led to private severance—this custom must not grow; the responsible office shall strictly establish penalties.
translations.idiomatic: But lately impeachments regardless of weight have led to private boycotts—this must not spread; penalties shall be strict.

sentences.zh: 」先是宋世江東貴達者，會稽孔季恭子靈符、吳興丘深之及琛，吳音不變。

translations.literal: Earlier among the noble and eminent of Jiangdong in the Song era—Kuaiji's Kong Jigong's son Lingfu, Wuxing's Qiu Shenzhi, and Chen—the Wu accent did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Among Song-era Jiangdong eminences—Kong Jigong's son Lingfu of Kuaiji, Qiu Shenzhi of Wuxing, and Chen—the Wu accent never changed.

sentences.zh: 深之字思玄，吳興烏程人，位侍中、都官尚書，卒于太常。

translations.literal: Shenzhi, courtesy name Siyuan, was a man of Wucheng in Wuxing; he held the posts of Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing for Punishments and died while Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi, styled Siyuan, came from Wucheng in Wuxing; he served as Palace Attendant and Director of Punishments and died as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 顧覬之字偉仁，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Gu Jizhi, courtesy name Weiren, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Jizhi, styled Weiren, came from Wu in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖謙字公讓，晉平原內史陸機姊夫。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qian, courtesy name Gongrang, was brother-in-law to Lu Ji, Interior Administrator of Pingyuan in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qian, styled Gongrang, was brother-in-law to Jin's Interior Administrator of Pingyuan, Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 祖崇，大司農。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chong was Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chong was Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 父黃老，司徒左西曹掾。

translations.literal: His father Huanglao was Aide in the Left Western Section of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huanglao was aide in the Minister of Education's left western section.

sentences.zh: 覬之為謝晦衛軍參軍，晦愛其雅素，深相知待。

translations.literal: Jizhi was a staff officer to Xie Hui's Guard General; Hui loved his refined simplicity and knew and treated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi served on Xie Hui's Guard General staff; Hui admired his refined simplicity and treated him with deep trust.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Gentleman in the Punishments Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman in the Punishments Section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 殷、劉隙著，覬之不欲與殷景仁久接，乃辭腳疾免歸。

translations.literal: When the rift between Yin and Liu became prominent, Jizhi did not wish prolonged contact with Yin Jingren and therefore pleaded foot ailment and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yin–Liu feud flared, Jizhi avoided prolonged contact with Yin Jingren, pleaded foot ailment, and retired home.

sentences.zh: 每夜常于床上行腳，家人竊異之而莫曉其意。

translations.literal: Each night he often walked his feet on the bed; the family secretly found it strange but none understood his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Each night he walked back and forth on his bed; the household found it strange but none guessed why.

sentences.zh: 及義康徙廢，朝廷多受禍。

translations.literal: When Yikang was transferred and deposed, many in court suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang was deposed and banished, many at court were ruined.

sentences.zh: 覬之竟免。

translations.literal: Jizhi entirely escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 後為山陰令。

translations.literal: Later he became Magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: He later became magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 山陰劇邑三萬戶，前後官長晝夜不得休，事猶不舉。

translations.literal: Shanyin was a difficult district of thirty thousand households; former magistrates day and night could not rest and still could not finish affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin was a demanding district of thirty thousand households; previous magistrates worked day and night yet still fell behind.

sentences.zh: 覬之禦繁以約，縣用無事。

translations.literal: Jizhi governed complexity through restraint; the district had no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi handled complexity through restraint; the district ran without crisis.

sentences.zh: 晝日垂簾，門階閑寂，自宋世為山陰，務簡而事理，莫能尚也。

translations.literal: By day he let the curtain hang; the gate and steps were quiet—since the Song era as magistrate of Shanyin, in simplifying affairs while managing reason, none could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: By day his curtain hung undisturbed and the gate steps were silent; since Song times no Shanyin magistrate matched his simplicity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Director of Personnel in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 嘗于文帝坐論江東人物，言及顧榮，袁淑謂覬之曰：「卿南人怯懦，豈辦作賊。

translations.literal: Once at Emperor Wen's seat he discussed figures of Jiangdong; speaking of Gu Rong, Yuan Shu said to Jizhi: "You southerners are timid and weak—how could you manage to be rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Once at Emperor Wen's court, discussing Jiangdong figures and Gu Rong, Yuan Shu told Jizhi, "You southerners are timid—how could you play rebels?"

sentences.zh: 」覬之正色曰：「卿乃復以忠義笑人。

translations.literal: Jizhi said with a stern face: "You again use loyalty and righteousness to mock people."
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi said gravely, "You mock men with their own loyalty and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」淑有愧色。

translations.literal: Shu had a ashamed face.
translations.idiomatic: Shu flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 孝建中，為湘州刺史，以政績稱。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian era he was Inspector of Xiang Province and was known for administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaojian era he governed Xiang Province and was praised for his record.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，征守度支尚書，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming he was summoned to serve as Director of the Masters of Writing for Revenue and transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming's first year he was summoned as Director of Revenue and transferred to Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時沛郡相縣唐賜往比村彭家飲酒還，因得病，吐蠱二十餘物。

translations.literal: At that time Tang Ci of Xiang County in Pei Commandery went to drink at the Peng household in a neighboring village and on returning fell ill, vomiting more than twenty parasitic creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Then Tang Ci of Pei's Xiang County drank at a neighbor's Peng household and returned home ill, vomiting more than twenty parasitic masses.

sentences.zh: 賜妻張從賜臨終言，死後親刳腹，五藏悉糜碎。

translations.literal: Ci's wife Zhang followed Ci's dying words: after death she would personally cut open the belly; the five viscera were all crushed to fragments.
translations.idiomatic: Ci's wife Zhang obeyed his dying wish and cut open his belly after death; all five viscera lay crushed.

sentences.zh: 郡縣以張忍行刳剖，賜子副又不禁止。

translations.literal: The commandery and county considered that Zhang endured performing cutting and dissection, and Ci's son Fu also did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery and county held that Zhang had endured mutilation and son Fu had not stopped her.

sentences.zh: 論妻傷夫，五歲刑，子不孝父母，子棄市。

translations.literal: They judged the wife for injuring her husband—five years' punishment; the son unfilial to parents—the son executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: They sentenced the wife to five years for injuring her husband and the son to market execution for unfiliality.

sentences.zh: 並非科例。

translations.literal: Neither was statutory precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Neither sentence matched statutory precedent.

sentences.zh: 三公郎劉勰議：「賜妻痛遵往言，兒識謝及理，考事原心，非在忍害，謂宜哀矜。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Three Ducal Offices Liu Xie argued: "Ci's wife painfully followed his former words; the son understood apology and reason; examining the matter according to intent, the harm was not in cruelty—they should be treated with compassion."
translations.idiomatic: Three Ducal Offices Gentleman Liu Xie argued: "The wife obeyed a dying command; the son grasped filial reason; judged by intent, not cruelty—they deserve compassion."

sentences.zh: 」覬之議：「以妻子而行忍酷，不宜曲通小情，謂副為不孝，張同不道。

translations.literal: Jizhi argued: "For wife and son to perform cruel forbearance, one should not bend small feeling; I consider Fu unfilial and Zhang equally impious."
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi argued: "Wife and son performed cruel obedience; sentiment must not bend the law—I hold Fu unfilial and Zhang equally impious."

sentences.zh: 」詔如覬之議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Jizhi's argument.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed Jizhi's view.

sentences.zh: 後為吳郡太守，幸臣戴法興權傾人主，而覬之未嘗低意。

translations.literal: Later he was Administrator of Wu Commandery; the favored minister Dai Faxing's power tilted over the ruler, yet Jizhi never lowered his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Later as Administrator of Wu Commandery, favored minister Dai Faxing overshadowed the throne, yet Jizhi never bowed.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫蔡興宗與覬之善，嫌其風節過峻。

translations.literal: Left Director of Splendid Honors Cai Xingzong was on good terms with Jizhi but disliked that his integrity was too severe.
translations.idiomatic: Left Director Cai Xingzong was Jizhi's friend yet thought his integrity too harsh.

sentences.zh: 覬之曰：「辛毗有雲，孫、劉不過使吾不為三公耳。

translations.literal: Jizhi said: "Xin Pi has a saying: Sun and Liu at most kept me from becoming one of the Three Ducal Offices."
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi said, "Xin Pi said Sun and Liu could at most keep me from the Three Ducal Offices."

sentences.zh: 」後卒于湘州刺史，諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: Later he died while Inspector of Xiang Province; his posthumous title was Master Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office as Inspector of Xiang Province; his posthumous title was Master Jian.

sentences.zh: 覬之家門雍穆，為州郡所重。

translations.literal: Jizhi's household was harmonious and solemn and was respected by provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's household was harmonious and solemn and won respect in every province and commandery.

sentences.zh: 子綽私財甚豐，鄉里士庶多負責，覬之禁不能止。

translations.literal: His son Chuo's private wealth was very abundant; many gentlemen and commoners in the district owed debts, and Jizhi forbade but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuo grew very wealthy; many locals owed him money, and Jizhi forbade it but could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 及後為吳郡，誘出文券一大廚，悉令焚之。

translations.literal: When later he was Administrator of Wu Commandery he lured out a great cupboard of written bonds and ordered them all burned.
translations.idiomatic: Later as Administrator of Wu Commandery he brought out a cupboard of debt bonds and burned them all.

sentences.zh: 宣語遠近，皆不須還。

translations.literal: He proclaimed to near and far that none need repay.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed near and far that no debts need be repaid.

sentences.zh: 綽懊歎彌日。

translations.literal: Chuo grieved and sighed for a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo grieved an entire day.

sentences.zh: 覬之常執命有定分，非智力所移，唯應恭己守道，信天任運。

translations.literal: Jizhi always held that fate has fixed allotment, not moved by intellect or strength; one should only respectfully keep the Way and trust Heaven and accept fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi held that fate is fixed, not moved by wit or force; one should keep the Way, trust Heaven, and accept what comes.

sentences.zh: 而闇者不達，妄意徼幸，徒虧雅道，無關得喪。

translations.literal: Yet the dark do not comprehend and vainly hope for luck; they only lose elegant conduct, unrelated to gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: The foolish hope for luck, lose elegant conduct, and gain nothing either way.

sentences.zh: 乃以其意，命弟子願作定命論。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered his disciple Yuan to compose the Treatise on Fixed Destiny according to his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore had his disciple Yuan compose the Treatise on Fixed Destiny from his views.

sentences.zh: 願字子恭，父深之，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Zigong; his father Shenzhi was Palace Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, styled Zigong, was son of Palace Gentleman Shenzhi.

sentences.zh: 願好學，有才辭，卒于太子舍人。

translations.literal: Yuan loved learning and had literary talent; he died while Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan loved learning and wrote well; he died as Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 覬之孫憲之。

translations.literal: Jizhi's grandson Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's grandson Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 憲之字士思，性尤清直。

translations.literal: Xianzhi, courtesy name Shisi, was by nature especially pure and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi, styled Shisi, was exceptionally upright and pure.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽中，為建康令。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era of Song he was Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Yuanhui era he was magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時有盜牛者，與本主爭牛，各稱己物，二家辭證等，前後令莫能決。

translations.literal: At that time there was a cattle thief who disputed oxen with the original owner; each claimed the beast as his own; the two households' arguments and evidence were equal, and former magistrates could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: A cattle thief disputed ownership with the true owner; arguments and evidence matched, and previous magistrates could not decide.

sentences.zh: 憲之至，覆其狀，乃令解牛任其所去，牛徑還本宅，盜者始伏其罪，時人號曰神明。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi arrived he reviewed the case and ordered the ox untied to go where it would; the ox went straight back to its original home and the thief at last confessed his crime; men of the time called him divine in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi reviewed the case, untied the ox, and let it choose; it walked straight home and the thief confessed—men called his judgment divine.

sentences.zh: 至於權要請托，長吏貪殘，據法直繩，無所阿縱。

translations.literal: As for powerful men's requests and entreaties, and senior officials' greed and cruelty, he applied the law straight and had no bending or indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Facing powerful men's requests and greedy senior officials, he applied the law straight without favor.

sentences.zh: 性又清儉，強力為政，甚得人和，故都下飲酒者醇旨輒號為「顧建康」，謂其清且美焉。

translations.literal: His nature was also pure and frugal; he governed forcefully and greatly won human harmony; therefore drinkers in the capital, when wine was pure and fine, would call it "Gu of Jiankang," saying it was both pure and excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and frugal, he governed forcefully and won popular trust; capital drinkers called fine wine "Gu of Jiankang"—pure and excellent.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為衡陽內史。

translations.literal: Serving Qi he was Interior Administrator of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as Interior Administrator of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，郡境連歲疾疫，死者太半，棺槨尤貴，悉裹以葦席，棄之路傍。

translations.literal: Earlier the commandery borders had plague year after year; more than half died; coffins were especially costly and all were wrapped in reed mats and cast beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: Plague had ravaged the commandery for years; more than half died; coffins were costly and corpses were wrapped in reed mats and left by the roads.

sentences.zh: 憲之下車，分告屬縣，求其親黨，悉令殯葬。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi took office he separately notified the subordinate counties to seek kin and ordered proper burial for all.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he ordered subordinate counties to find kin and bury every body properly.

sentences.zh: 其家人絕滅者，憲之出公祿使紀綱營護之。

translations.literal: Where families were extinct, Xianzhi disbursed official salary and had his clerks arrange care.
translations.idiomatic: Where families were extinct he spent official funds and had clerks arrange burial.

sentences.zh: 又土俗：山人有病輒云先亡為禍，皆開塚剖棺，水洗枯骨，名為除祟。

translations.literal: Also local custom: when mountain people fell ill they said the dead ancestors brought disaster; all opened tombs, cut open coffins, washed dry bones with water—called "removing malign influence."
translations.idiomatic: Local custom held that illness came from dead ancestors; people opened tombs, cut coffins, and washed bones—"removing malign influence."

sentences.zh: 憲之曉喻，為陳生死之別，事不相由，風俗遂改。

translations.literal: Xianzhi enlightened them, set forth the distinction between life and death and that affairs do not connect; the custom was thus changed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi explained life and death's separation and that the living and dead do not cause one another's ills; the custom changed.

sentences.zh: 時刺史王奐初至，唯衡陽獨無訟者，乃歎曰：「顧衡陽之化至矣，若九郡率然，吾將何事。」

translations.literal: At that time Inspector Wang Huan had just arrived; only Hengyang had no lawsuits, and he sighed: "Gu of Hengyang's transformation has reached this point; if the nine commanderies were all thus, what would I have to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Huan, newly arrived, found only Hengyang free of lawsuits and sighed, "Gu of Hengyang's transformation is complete; if all nine commanderies were thus, what work would remain for me?"

sentences.zh: 後為東中郎長史，行會稽郡事。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Administrator to the Eastern General of the Center and acted for Kuaiji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief administrator to the Eastern General of the Center and acting administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 山陰人呂文度有寵于齊武帝，于余姚立邸，頗縱橫。

translations.literal: Lü Wendu of Shanyin enjoyed favor with Emperor Wu of Qi and established a lodge at Yuyao, behaving quite lawlessly.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin's Lü Wendu, favored by Qi Emperor Wu, built a lodge at Yuyao and behaved lawlessly.

sentences.zh: 憲之至郡，即日除之。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi reached the commandery he abolished it the same day.
translations.idiomatic: The day Xianzhi reached the commandery he abolished it.

sentences.zh: 文度後還葬，郡縣爭赴吊，憲之不與相聞，文度甚銜之，亦卒不能傷也。

translations.literal: Wendu later returned for burial; commanderies and counties competed to attend condolences; Xianzhi did not communicate with him; Wendu greatly resented it but in the end could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu later returned for burial; counties rushed to mourn; Xianzhi sent no word; Wendu resented it but could not touch him.

sentences.zh: 時西陵戍主杜元懿以吳興歲儉，會稽年登，商旅往來倍歲。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison commander of Xiling, Du Yuanyi, because Wuxing had a lean year while Kuaiji had a good harvest, merchant travel doubled over the year.
translations.idiomatic: Xiling garrison commander Du Yuanyi noted Wuxing's lean year against Kuaiji's harvest and doubled merchant traffic.

sentences.zh: 西陵牛埭稅，官格日三千五百，求加至一倍，計年長百萬。

translations.literal: The Xiling ox-ford tax, by official rate three thousand five hundred per day, he sought to increase to double, calculating an annual surplus of a million.
translations.idiomatic: Xiling's ox-ford tax stood at three thousand five hundred per day by statute; he sought to double it for a million in annual surplus.

sentences.zh: 浦陽南北津及柳浦四埭，乞為官領攝，一年格外長四百許萬。

translations.literal: The Puyang north and south crossings and the four fords of Liupu—he begged to take official charge, with an annual surplus beyond the quota of about four million.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought charge of Puyang's crossings and Liupu's four fords for four million beyond quota.

sentences.zh: 武帝以示會稽，使陳得失。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu showed this to Kuaiji and had them set forth gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent the proposal to Kuaiji for comment on gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 憲之議曰：

translations.literal: Xianzhi argued:
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi argued:

sentences.zh: 尋始立牛埭，非苟通僦以納稅也，當以風濤迅險，人力不捷，濟急以利物耳。

translations.literal: Seeking the original establishment of the ox-ford, it was not casually to pass rentals and collect tax; it was because wind and waves were swift and dangerous and human strength could not be quick—to aid urgency and benefit things.
translations.idiomatic: The ox-ford was not established merely to collect tolls but because swift dangerous waters exceeded human strength—to aid urgent crossing and benefit travelers.

sentences.zh: 既公私是樂，故輸直無怨。

translations.literal: Since public and private alike rejoiced in it, the ferry fee was paid without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private alike welcomed it, so ferry fees drew no complaint.

sentences.zh: 京師航渡，即其例也。

translations.literal: Capital river crossings are the example.
translations.idiomatic: Capital river crossings follow the same principle.

sentences.zh: 而後之監領，各務己功，或禁遏別道，互生理外，凡如此類，不經埭煩牛者上詳。

translations.literal: But later overseers each pursued their own achievement, or blocked alternate routes and mutually created profit outside regulations; all such cases of not passing the ford and troubling oxen were reported upward in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Later overseers pursued private gain, blocked alternate routes, and created extralegal profits; every evasion of the ford was reported upward.

sentences.zh: 被報蒙停格外十條，從來喧訴，始得暫弭。

translations.literal: The reply granted suspension of ten items beyond quota; clamor and suits from former times then briefly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial reply suspended ten extralegal charges; long-standing clamor briefly ceased.

sentences.zh: 案吳興頻歲失稔，今茲尤饉，去乏從豐，良田饑棘，舊格新減，尚未議登，格外加倍，將以何術？

translations.literal: Wuxing has repeatedly had poor harvests; this year famine is especially severe—going from want to plenty, good fields to hungry thorns; old rates newly reduced have not yet been discussed for restoration, yet beyond-quota doubling—by what method?
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing has suffered repeated poor harvests; famine this year is worst yet—good fields turn to thorns; old rates were cut and not restored, yet he would double beyond-quota charges—by what means?

sentences.zh: 皇慈恤隱，振廩蠲調，而元懿幸災榷利，重增困瘼，人而不仁，古今共疾。

translations.literal: Imperial kindness pities the hidden and afflicted, opens granaries and remits levies, yet Yuanyi profiteers from disaster and heavily adds to distress—inhumanity condemned in all ages.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kindness opens granaries and remits levies, yet Yuanyi profiteers from disaster and deepens distress—inhumanity condemned in every age.

sentences.zh: 且比見加格置市者，前後相屬，非唯新加無贏，並皆舊格有闕，愚恐元懿今啟，亦當不殊。

translations.literal: Moreover comparing recent cases of establishing beyond-quota markets, one after another—not only do new additions yield no surplus, but old rates also fall short; I fear Yuanyi's present proposal will likewise not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Recent beyond-quota markets have multiplied—not only failing to yield surplus but falling short of old rates; Yuanyi's proposal will likely fare no better.

sentences.zh: 若事不副言，懼貽譴詰，便百方侵苦，為公賈怨，其所欲舉腹心，亦當獸而冠耳。

translations.literal: If affairs do not match words, I fear reproof and inquiry; then a hundred ways of oppression and suffering will buy public resentment for the lord, and the trusted men he wishes to appoint will also be beasts wearing caps.
translations.idiomatic: If results fail to match promises, inquiry will follow; oppression will buy public resentment, and his chosen agents will be beasts in human dress.

sentences.zh: 書云：「與其有聚斂之臣，寧有盜臣。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Better have a thieving minister than a minister who gathers wealth."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, "Better a thieving minister than one who gathers wealth."

sentences.zh: 」言盜公為損蓋微，斂人所害乃大也。

translations.literal: It means theft from the public causes slight harm, but gathering from the people causes great harm.
translations.idiomatic: Theft from the public harms little; gathering from the people harms greatly.

sentences.zh: 然掌斯任者應簡廉平，則無害於人。

translations.literal: Yet those who hold this charge should be selected for integrity and fairness, then there is no harm to people.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold such posts should be chosen for integrity and fairness, then people suffer no harm.

sentences.zh: 愚又以便宜者，蓋謂便於公宜於人也。

translations.literal: Your servant also considers that "convenience" means what is convenient for the public and suitable for the people.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that "convenience" means what serves the public and suits the people.

sentences.zh: 竊見頃之言便宜者，非能於人力之外，用天分地者也，率皆即日不宜於人，方來未便於公，名與實反，有乖政體。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that those who lately speak of convenience are not using heaven's allotment and earth's division beyond human power; almost all are unsuitable for people today and will not be convenient for the public tomorrow—name and fact oppose each other and violate the body of government.
translations.idiomatic: Lately "convenience" means neither heaven's allotment nor earth's division—it harms people today and the public tomorrow; name and fact diverge and violate good government.

sentences.zh: 凡如此等，誠宜深察。

translations.literal: All such cases truly should be deeply examined.
translations.idiomatic: All such cases deserve deep scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 山陰一縣課戶二萬，其人貲不滿三千者，殆將居半，刻又刻之，猶且三分餘一。

translations.literal: Shanyin one county has twenty thousand taxable households; of these those whose property does not reach three thousand nearly half; carved and carved again, still a third and more remain.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin alone has twenty thousand taxable households; nearly half hold property under three thousand—carved again and again, still a third remain.

sentences.zh: 凡有貲者多是士人復除，其貧極者悉皆露戶役人，三五屬官，蓋惟分定，百端輸調，又則常然。

translations.literal: Generally those with property are mostly gentlemen enjoying exemption; the extremely poor are all bare households serving corvée; three or five attached to officials—this is allotted division; a hundred kinds of levies and transport—again this is constant.
translations.idiomatic: The propertied are mostly exempt gentlemen; the poorest are bare households on corvée; three or five attached to officials is fixed allotment; countless levies are constant.

sentences.zh: 比眾局檢校，首尾尋續，橫相質累者亦復不少。

translations.literal: Recently the many bureaus inspect and verify, tracing head to tail in succession; those mutually implicated across cases are also not few.
translations.idiomatic: Recently bureaus inspect endlessly; cross-case implications are not few.

sentences.zh: 一人被攝，十人相追，一緒裁萌，千孽互起。

translations.literal: One person seized, ten people pursue; one thread just sprouting, a thousand evils rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Seize one man and ten pursue; one thread sprouts and a thousand evils follow.

sentences.zh: 蠶事弛而農業廢，賤取庸而貴舉責，應公贍私，日不暇給，欲無為非，其可得乎。

translations.literal: Silkworm work slackens and agriculture is abandoned; cheap hired labor and dear debt collection; answering public needs from private funds—days without surplus; wishing not to do wrong—how can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Silkworm work slackens and farming fails; cheap labor and dear debt; public duty drains private means daily—who can stay honest?

sentences.zh: 死且不憚，矧伊刑罰，身且不愛，何況妻子。

translations.literal: They do not fear death—how much less punishment; they do not love their own bodies—how much less wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Men who fear not death fear punishment less still; who love not their bodies love wives and children less still.

sentences.zh: 是以前檢未窮，後巧復滋，網辟徒峻，猶不能悛。

translations.literal: Therefore before one inspection ends, new tricks again multiply; though the net is only stern, they still cannot reform.
translations.idiomatic: Before one inspection ends new evasions multiply; though the net grows stern, men will not reform.

sentences.zh: 竊尋人之多偽，實由宋季軍旅繁興，役賦殷重，不堪勤劇，奇巧所優，積習生常，遂迷忘反。

translations.literal: Your servant seeks the reason people's falsity is abundant: truly because in the Song end military campaigns were frequent and corvée and levies heavy; unable to bear labor and urgency, they excelled in strange cleverness; accumulated habit became constant and they lost their way in reversal.
translations.idiomatic: Men falsify because late Song campaigns and heavy levies drove them to clever evasion; habit hardened into custom and they forgot the straight path.

sentences.zh: 四海之大，庶黎之眾，心用參差，難卒澄之。

translations.literal: Within the four seas the multitude of the people—hearts and uses differ; hard suddenly to clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Within the four seas hearts differ; sudden clarification is impossible.

sentences.zh: 化宜以漸，不可疾責。

translations.literal: Transformation should be gradual; one cannot urgently demand.
translations.idiomatic: Reform should be gradual; haste avails nothing.

sentences.zh: 誠存不擾，藏疾納洿。

translations.literal: Truly preserve non-disturbance; hide illness and accept filth.
translations.idiomatic: Preserve non-disturbance; tolerate flaws and accept imperfection.

sentences.zh: 務詳寬簡，則稍自歸淳。

translations.literal: Devote effort to leniency and simplicity, then gradually they return to purity.
translations.idiomatic: Devote effort to leniency and simplicity, and men gradually return to honesty.

sentences.zh: 又被簡符，前後累千，符旨既嚴，不敢闇信。

translations.literal: Also receiving inspection orders, front and back numbering in the thousands; the order's intent being stern, one dare not blindly believe.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection orders arrive by the thousand; their stern intent forbids blind compliance.

sentences.zh: 縣簡送郡，郡簡呈使，殊形詭狀，千變萬源。

translations.literal: County orders sent to commandery, commandery orders presented to commissioner— strange forms and deceitful shapes, a thousand changes and ten thousand sources.
translations.idiomatic: County sends to commandery, commandery to commissioner—strange forms and deceitful shapes in endless variety.

sentences.zh: 聞者忽不經懷，見者實足傷駭。

translations.literal: Hearing them one suddenly pays no heed; seeing them truly enough to wound and shock.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing them one pays no heed; seeing them one is shocked.

sentences.zh: 兼親屬裏伍，流離道路，時轉窮涸，事方未已，其士人婦女彌難厝衷。

translations.literal: Moreover kin and neighborhood wards wander on the roads, sometimes turning destitute; the affair is not yet ended—the gentry's women find it especially hard to place their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and neighbors wander the roads toward destitution; the affair is not ended—and gentry women suffer most.

sentences.zh: 不簡則疑其有巧，欲簡復未知所安。

translations.literal: Not inspecting then suspects them of trickery; wishing to inspect again one does not know what is safe.
translations.idiomatic: Skip inspection and one suspects trickery; inspect and one knows not what is safe.

sentences.zh: 愚謂此條宜委縣保，舉其綱領，略其毛目，乃當有漏，不出貯中，庶嬰疾沈痼者重荷生造之恩也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this item should be entrusted to county guarantors, raising the main cord and omitting fine threads—then there will be leaks not escaping the storehouse; perhaps those with deep chronic illness will again bear the grace of renewed life.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust this to county guarantors— grasp the main cord, omit fine threads—then leaks stay within bounds and the chronically afflicted may breathe again.

sentences.zh: 又永興、諸暨離唐宇寇擾，公私殘燼，彌復特甚，儻逢水旱，實不易思。

translations.literal: Also Yongxing and Zhuji, having left Tang's domain, suffered bandit disturbance; public and private were burned to embers, especially severe again; if flood or drought should come, it is truly not easy to contemplate.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing and Zhuji, ravaged after leaving Tang's domain, lie burned bare; flood or drought would be unbearable to contemplate.

sentences.zh: 俗諺云：「會稽打鼓送恤，吳興步擔令史。

translations.literal: A popular saying goes: "Kuaiji beats drums to send relief; Wuxing carries the clerk's dispatch on a shoulder pole."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says, "Kuaiji beats drums to send relief; Wuxing carries the clerk's dispatch on a shoulder pole."

sentences.zh: 」會稽舊稱沃壤，今猶若此，吳興本是塉土，事在可知。

translations.literal: Kuaiji was formerly called fertile soil; even now it is thus; Wuxing was originally barren land—the matter is knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji was once called fertile; even now it struggles; Wuxing was always poor soil—the contrast tells all.

sentences.zh: 因循餘弊，誠宜改張。

translations.literal: Following remaining abuses, truly reform should be spread.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining abuses cry out for reform.

sentences.zh: 武帝並從之，由是深以方直見知。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu all followed this; by this he was deeply known for square integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu accepted every point; Xianzhi won deep renown for upright integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷南中郎巴陵王長史、南兗南豫二州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred Chief Administrator to the Southern General of the Center Prince of Baling and charged with the two provinces of Southern Yan and Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief administrator to Prince of Baling, Southern General of the Center, charged with Southern Yan and Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 典簽諮事，未嘗接以顏色，動遵法制。

translations.literal: For registry clerks consulting on business he never met them with a pleasant face and always moved according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Registry clerks never saw a pleasant face from him; he moved strictly by law.

sentences.zh: 時司徒竟陵王于宣城、臨成、定陵三縣界立屯，封山澤數百里，禁人樵采。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Prince of Jingling established garrisons at the borders of Xuancheng, Lincheng, and Dingling counties, sealing mountains and marshes for several hundred li and forbidding people to gather firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Prince of Jingling established garrisons across Xuancheng, Lincheng, and Dingling, sealing hundreds of li of mountains and marshes and forbidding firewood gathering.

sentences.zh: 憲之固陳不可，言甚切直。

translations.literal: Xianzhi firmly stated it was impossible; his words were very direct.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi firmly protested in blunt, direct words.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「非君無以聞此德音。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Without you I would not have heard this virtuous word."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Without you I would never have heard this righteous counsel."

sentences.zh: 」即命罷屯禁。

translations.literal: He at once ordered the garrisons and prohibitions abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He at once abolished the garrisons and prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門，兼尚書吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, concurrently Gentleman in the Personnel Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Gentleman in the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 宋時其祖覬之嘗為吏部，於庭列植嘉樹，謂人曰：「吾為憲之植耳。

translations.literal: In Song times his grandfather Jizhi had once been Director of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted fine trees and told people: "I am planting for Xianzhi."
translations.idiomatic: In Song times his grandfather Jizhi, once Director of Personnel, planted fine trees in the courtyard and said, "I plant these for Xianzhi."

sentences.zh: 」至是憲之果為此職。

translations.literal: At this Xianzhi indeed held this office.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xianzhi indeed held that office.

sentences.zh: 永元中為豫章內史，在任清簡，務存寬惠。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era he was Interior Administrator of Yuzhang; in office he was pure and simple and devoted effort to leniency and grace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongyuan era he governed Yuzhang with purity and simplicity, devoted to leniency and grace.

sentences.zh: 有貞婦萬晞者，少孀居無子，事舅姑尤孝，父母欲奪而嫁之，誓死不許。

translations.literal: There was a chaste woman Wan Xi who widowed young without sons and served her parents-in-law with especial filial piety; her parents wished to force her to remarry and she swore she would rather die.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste woman Wan Xi widowed young and childless, served her in-laws with deep filial piety, and refused remarriage though her parents insisted, swearing to die first.

sentences.zh: 憲之賜以束帛，表其節義。

translations.literal: Xianzhi bestowed silk rolls and memorialized her integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi bestowed silk rolls and memorialized her integrity.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝平建鄴，為揚州牧，征憲之為別駕從事史，比至而已受禪。

translations.literal: When Liang Emperor Wu pacified Jiankang he was Governor of Yang Province and summoned Xianzhi as Assistant Administrator and Staff Officer; by the time he arrived the Emperor had already received the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Wu pacified Jiankang as Governor of Yang Province he summoned Xianzhi as assistant administrator; by the time Xianzhi arrived the emperor had already taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 憲之風疾漸篤，因求還吳，就加太中大夫。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's wind ailment gradually worsened; he therefore requested return to Wu and was concurrently promoted Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's palsy worsened; he asked to return to Wu and was promoted Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 憲之雖累經宰郡，資無儋石，及歸，環堵不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Though Xianzhi had repeatedly governed commanderies he had no store of a hundred dan; when he returned, his ring of walls could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had governed many commanderies he owned no store of grain; home again, his bare walls could not keep out hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 天監八年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianjian he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian's eighth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 臨終為制敕其子曰：「夫出生入死，理均晝夜。

translations.literal: Facing death he made regulations instructing his sons: "Birth and entering death—reason equally divides day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he instructed his sons: "Birth and death divide life as day divides night.

sentences.zh: 生既不知所從，死亦安識所往。

translations.literal: Life already not knowing whence it comes, death also how can one know whither it goes.
translations.idiomatic: Life—we know not whence it comes; death—we know not whither it goes.

sentences.zh: 延陵云：'精氣上歸於天，骨肉下歸於地，魂氣則無所不之。

translations.literal: Yanling said: 'Essence and spirit return upward to heaven, flesh and bone return downward to earth, soul and breath then go everywhere.'
translations.idiomatic: Yanling said: 'Essence rises to heaven, flesh returns to earth, soul and breath wander everywhere.'"

sentences.zh: ' 良有以也。

translations.literal: Truly there is reason in this.
translations.idiomatic: There is reason in that.

sentences.zh: 雖復茫昧難征，要若非妄。

translations.literal: Though again obscure and hard to verify, essentially it is not vain.
translations.idiomatic: Though obscure and hard to verify, it is not vain.

sentences.zh: 百年之期，迅若馳隙，吾今預為終制，瞑目之後，念並遵行，勿違吾志也。

translations.literal: A hundred years' term, swift as a galloping gap; I now beforehand make final regulations—after closing the eyes, think all and follow in conduct; do not violate my will.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred years pass like a galloping gap; I now set final rules—after my eyes close, follow them all and do not violate my will.

sentences.zh: 莊周、澹台，達生者也；

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou and Dantai were men who comprehended life;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Zhou and Dantai comprehended life;

sentences.zh: 王孫、士安，矯俗者也。

translations.literal: Wang Sun and Shi'an were men who corrected custom.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sun and Shi'an corrected custom.

sentences.zh: 吾進不及達，退無所矯。

translations.literal: My advance did not reach comprehension; my retreat had nothing to correct.
translations.idiomatic: I neither reached their comprehension nor their corrective zeal.

sentences.zh: 常謂中都之制，允理愜情，衣周於身，示不違禮，棺周於衣，足以蔽臭。

translations.literal: I always considered the regulations of the central capital permissible in reason and satisfying in feeling—clothes wrapping the body show not violating ritual; coffin wrapping the clothes suffices to cover stench.
translations.idiomatic: I always held the capital's rites reasonable and satisfying—clothes on the body show ritual kept; a coffin around the clothes suffices to cover decay.

sentences.zh: 入棺之物，一無所須，載以輴車，覆以粗布，為使人勿惡也。

translations.literal: Objects entering the coffin—nothing is needed; carry on the plain cart, cover with coarse cloth, so that people will not be disgusted.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing need enter the coffin; carry me on a plain cart covered with coarse cloth so men need not be disgusted.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝天子之尊，猶祭以杅水脯糗，范史雲列士之高，亦奠以寒水乾飯。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Han, though the Son of Heaven's honor, still sacrificed with earthen cup, water, dried meat and parched grain; Fan Shiyun, though an exemplary knight of lofty standing, also offered cold water and dry rice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Han, though Son of Heaven, sacrificed with earthen cup, water, and parched grain; Fan Shiyun, though a lofty gentleman, offered cold water and dry rice.

sentences.zh: 況吾卑庸之人，其可不節衷也。

translations.literal: How much more for a base and mediocre man like me—can he not restrain inner feeling?
translations.idiomatic: How much more should a base man like me restrain extravagance?

sentences.zh: 喪易甯戚，自是親親之情，禮奢寧儉，差可得由吾意。

translations.literal: Changing mourning is easier than settling grief—this is naturally affection for kin; ritual extravagant, better frugal—one can somewhat follow my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Easing mourning is easier than settling grief—that is natural kin affection; when ritual tends toward extravagance, choose frugality and you may follow my intent.

sentences.zh: 不須常施靈筵，可止設香燈，使致哀者有憑耳。

translations.literal: Do not constantly set spirit tables; stop at setting incense lamps, so those who express grief have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Do not constantly set spirit tables; incense lamps alone will give mourners something to rely on.

sentences.zh: 朔望祥忌，可權安小床，暫施幾席，唯下素饌，勿用牲牢。

translations.literal: New and full moon and auspicious and taboo days— temporarily set a small bed and briefly place stools and mats; only set plain food, do not use sacrificial animals.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moons and memorial days, set a small bed briefly with plain mats and plain food only—no sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 蒸嘗之祠，貴賤罔替，備物難辦，多致疏怠。

translations.literal: Seasonal ancestral sacrifices—noble and base none replaced—preparing objects is hard to manage and much leads to neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal ancestral rites bind noble and base alike; elaborate offerings are hard to maintain and invite neglect.

sentences.zh: 祠先自有舊典，不可有闕，自吾已下，止用蔬食時果，勿同於上世，示令子孫四時不忘其親耳。

translations.literal: Sacrificing to ancestors naturally has old statutes and cannot be lacking; from me downward use only vegetables, seasonal fruit—do not match the upper generation, showing descendants the four seasons do not forget their kin.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestors' rites have old statutes and must not lapse; from my generation down use vegetables and seasonal fruit only—not matching elders' lavish rites, so descendants remember kin through the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 孔子雲'雖菜羹瓜祭必齋如'者，本貴誠敬，豈求備物哉。

translations.literal: Confucius said 'though vegetable soup and melon sacrifice one must fast as if present'—originally valuing sincere reverence, how is it seeking prepared objects?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Even for vegetable soup and melon one must fast as if present'—sincere reverence matters, not lavish offerings.

sentences.zh: 」所著詩賦銘贊並衡陽郡記數十篇。

translations.literal: His composed poetry, rhapsodies, inscriptions, eulogies, and several tens of juan of Record of Hengyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He left poetry, rhapsodies, inscriptions, eulogies, and several tens of juan of Record of Hengyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古人云：「利令智昏」，甚矣利害之相傾也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The ancients said: "Profit makes wisdom dull"—how extreme is the mutual overturning of benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: The ancients said, "Profit dulls wisdom"—how extreme is the overturning of benefit and harm.

sentences.zh: 劉湛識用才能，實包經國之略，豈知移弟為臣，則君臣之道用，變兄成主，則兄弟之義殊。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan's discernment and talent in ability truly wrapped strategies for governing the state—who would know that shifting younger brother to minister then the way of ruler and minister applies, changing elder brother to lord then the righteousness of elder and younger brothers differs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan's talent truly held statecraft—yet when a younger brother becomes minister the ruler-minister way applies, and when an elder brother becomes lord brotherhood itself changes.

sentences.zh: 而執數懷奸，苟相崇悅，與夫推長戟而犯順，何以異哉。

translations.literal: Yet holding several schemes and harboring treachery, casually mutually exalting and pleasing—what difference from pushing the long halberd and violating obedience?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he clung to schemes and treachery, flattering power—how differs that from raising the halberd against one's lord?

sentences.zh: 昔華元敗則以羊羹而取禍，觀夫庾悅亦鵝炙以速尤。

translations.literal: Formerly Hua Yuan was defeated and met disaster through mutton broth; observing Yu Yue, goose roast also brought swift blame.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yuan's defeat brought disaster through mutton broth; Yu Yue's goose roast brought swift blame likewise.

sentences.zh: 幹餱以愆，斯相類矣。

translations.literal: Dry rations to fault—this is of the same kind.
translations.idiomatic: Fault over dry rations—the pattern repeats.

sentences.zh: 登之因禍而福，倚伏無常，仲文賄而為災，乃徇財之過也。

translations.literal: Dengzhi turned calamity into blessing— lying and rising have no constancy; Zhongwen's bribes became disaster— that is the fault of following wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi turned calamity to blessing— fortune and misfortune turn without rule; Zhongwen's bribes became disaster—the price of chasing wealth.

sentences.zh: 顧琛吳郡，徵兆于初筮，覬之清白之跡，見於暮年。

translations.literal: Gu Chen's Wu Commandery— omen at the first divination; Jizhi's pure white traces— seen in his late years.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen's Wu Commandery post was foretold at the first omen; Jizhi's pure conduct showed clearest in old age.

sentences.zh: 憲之蒞政，所在稱美，時移三代，一德無虧，求之古人，未為易遇。

translations.literal: Xianzhi governing wherever he arrived was praised; time moved through three generations, one virtue without loss— seeking this in ancients, it is not easily encountered.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi won praise wherever he governed; three generations passed without stain—such constancy is rare even among ancients.

sentences.zh: 觀其遺命，可謂有始有卒者矣。

translations.literal: Observing his final testament, one may say he had beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Reading his final testament, one may say he finished as he began.
